items.title: Opoku-Agyemang delivers keynote address at Sister Cities International 70th anniversary
items.description: Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has delivered the keynote address at the 70th anniversary celebration of Sister Cities International in Washington, DC. Sister Cities International, founded in 1956, is a non-profit network headquartered in Washington, DC, that connects communities in the United States with global partners through cultural, educational and trade exchanges. A statement issued by the Office of the Vice President said Prof Opoku-Agyemang, speaking on the theme: “Forging Stronger Partnerships in Africa for Sustainable Economic Development,” underscored the importance of city-to-city diplomacy in advancing development, strengthening institutions and fostering international relationships. “City-to-city partnerships continue to provide solutions to shared challenges and create opportunities for investment and mutual learning,” Vice President Prof Opoku-Agyemang said. She reiterated Ghana’s commitment to strengthening local governance through decentralisation and noted that under President John Dramani Mahama’s Reset Agenda, Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies remained central to national development. The Vice President explained that the Assemblies were being empowered with greater resources and responsibilities to improve the delivery of quality education, healthcare, infrastructure and other essential public services. Prof Opoku-Agyemang also highlighted Ghana’s strategic role as host of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat and pointed to the vast opportunities for inter-city collaboration across the continent. She said city diplomacy had the potential to stimulate trade, entrepreneurship, innovation, digital transformation and investment, while creating opportunities for the youth. The Vice President noted that cultural and educational exchanges remained critical to building trust and strengthening bonds between communities. She said Ghana’s long-standing commitment to reconnecting with the African diaspora demonstrated how people-to-people engagement could develop into enduring partnerships that contributed significantly to development. “As cities worldwide face common challenges, including rapid urbanisation, climate change, waste management, public health, and disaster preparedness, we need greater collaboration among municipalities to share knowledge, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop practical solutions that enhance our quality of life,” Vice President Prof Opoku-Agyemang stated. Prof Opoku-Agyemang congratulated Sister Cities International on its 70 years of promoting global friendship and cooperation and reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to partnerships that advanced sustainable development, institutional learning, economic opportunity and shared prosperity.

items.title: Contrats d’objectifs : Yacouba Zabré Gouba affiche 61,7 % de réalisations, Mikaïlou Sidibé atteint 46 % à mi-parcours
items.description: Le Premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a reçu deux membres de son Gouvernement pour l’évaluation à mi-parcours de leurs contrats d’objectifs, le samedi 26 juillet 2026. Si le ministre de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, et le ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, Mikaïlou Sidibé, ont tous deux enregistré des avancées notables dans leurs secteurs respectifs, leurs taux d’exécution physique révèlent des dynamiques différentes. L’exercice de redevabilité bat son plein au sein du Gouvernement burkinabè. Pour le dernier balet ce samedi, c’est au tour de deux ministres techniques de défendre leur bilan semestriel devant le Chef du Gouvernement. Si les deux départements ministériels affichent des résultats jugés « satisfaisants » par leurs titulaires, les chiffres et les priorités divergent. Avec un taux de réalisation physique de 61,7 % au 30 juin 2026, le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba affiche l’un des meilleurs scores du Gouvernement. Ce résultat est porté par des avancées concrètes dans ses deux principaux domaines d’action. Sur le plan minier, l’accent mis sur l’artisanat et l’industrie porte ses fruits. Le ministère en charge des Mines a délimité quatre nouveaux couloirs d’exploitation artisanale et mis en place neuf coopératives minières, contribuant à une meilleure structuration du secteur. Cette régulation a permis de collecter près de 29 tonnes d’or via la SONASP (sur une prévision annuelle de 45 tonnes), tandis que les 15 mines industrielles ont produit environ 26 tonnes d’or fin. Ces chiffres illustrent la volonté du gouvernement de lutter contre la fraude et de maximiser les retombées économiques du sous-sol burkinabè. Côté énergie, le ministre Gouba a mis en avant les investissements massifs qui renforcent la souveraineté nationale. Quatre nouvelles centrales (trois thermiques et une solaire) ont été achevées, ajoutant près de 143 MW au réseau électrique national, avec d’autres chantiers d’envergure comme les centrales de Komsilga et Donsin en cours d’achèvement. Des infrastructures routières et une gouvernance foncière en chantier De son côté, le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé présente un taux d’exécution physique de 46 %, un score qu’il entend améliorer d’ici la fin de l’année. Son bilan est marqué par des réalisations palpables sur le terrain, notamment dans le secteur des transports et de l’urbanisme. Le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé a souligné l’achèvement du pont de Hèrèdougou sur la RN1, un ouvrage stratégique, ainsi que la reconstruction quasi totale de l’ouvrage de Bama, victime des intempéries. Les travaux se poursuivent sur plusieurs axes majeurs, comme la réhabilitation de la RN7 (tronçon Bobo-Banfora) et le bitumage de l’axe Banfora-Orodara, pour lesquels des aménagements provisoires ont déjà été mis en place. En matière de gouvernance urbaine, une réforme de fond a été engagée avec l’adoption du nouveau Code de l’urbanisme et de la construction, visant à simplifier les démarches et à digitaliser les autorisations de construire. En parallèle, le ministre Sidibé a annoncé le lancement d’une phase pilote de restructuration des quartiers spontanés à Ouagadougou et Bobo-Dioulasso, dans le cadre du programme d’apurement du passif foncier urbain. Si les deux ministres ont reçu les encouragements du Premier ministre, leurs feuilles de route pour le second semestre se dessinent différemment. Yacouba Zabré Gouba compte accélérer la cadence sur tous les chantiers pour faire des ressources minières et énergétiques un véritable levier de développement, en s’appuyant sur une dynamique déjà bien engagée. Mikaïlou Sidibé, quant à lui, mise sur l’intensification de la production de logements et l’extension des opérations de restructuration foncière pour améliorer son taux de réalisation d’ici décembre, en insistant sur l’amélioration de la mobilité et de l’accès à un habitat décent pour les populations. Jean François SOMÉ Minute.bf

items.title: Joshua survives knockdowns, stops Prenga
items.description: Two-time heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua survived two early knockdowns on the way to a second-round knockout of Kristian Prenga on Sunday, his triumphant ring return paving the way for a blockbuster all-British bout with Tyson Fury. The fight at the Jeddah Superdome was Joshua’s first since he was involved in a car crash in Nigeria in December that killed two of his close friends, Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele. The 36-year-old choked up when asked in the ring about his friends and the emotions of the past seven months, but said his second-round revival was down to more than pure punching power. “That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina. That was family,” he said. The devastating accident occurred little more than a week after Joshua demolished YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in a controversial Netflix-backed bout in December. Joshua’s last prior competitive appearance in the ring was his fifth-round knockout loss to IBF world champion Daniel Dubois at Wembley Stadium in September 2024. He improved to 30-4, with 27 wins by knockout, but not without drama. Albania’s Prenga, a knockout artist who had 20 wins inside the distance in 21 prior fights, sent Joshua to the canvas with a right uppercut just 20 seconds into the bout. He had Joshua on the ropes again, his legs shaky, before sending him down a second time late in the first round. But Joshua steadied in the second, backing Prenga into the corner behind his jab, shrugging off more heavy blows from the Albanian before inflicting damage of his own with his left hand. A brutal combination capped by a big right finally sent Prenga crashing through the ropes to end it at 2:43 of the second round. Joshua and Fury now appear set for their “Battle of Britain” in November, at a venue still to be announced. Fury, like Joshua a former two-time heavyweight world champion, did his part to make the long-anticipated fight happen, stopping Mariusz Wach in a low-key bout in Pattaya, Thailand, on Friday. Fury, 37, outclassed Wach in front in the Thai resort city, chipping away relentlessly at the 46-year-old until he was pulled out by his corner in the seventh round. It was Fury’s second win in as many contests this year in his return from a 16-month layoff. – ‘We’re here now’ – Fury wasn’t ringside in Jeddah as many had anticipated, but Joshua had a message for him even so. “I’m gonna rip his heart out! I’m the meanest, most vicious champion that has ever been. Nobody can stop me,” he said. “All jokes aside, there’s two sides of this thing,” Joshua added. “One is fire. You have to have that vim, that (roar). But also, there’s respect. “I respect everything he has done and everything that he has achieved. “But as a fighting person and someone who has been calling for this fight for a long time, we’re here now.” Promoter Eddie Hearn, also speaking inside the ring in the wake of the bout streamed on DAZN, said the contract to fight Fury was signed. “Everything’s done,” Hearn said. “But to be honest with you, tonight is all about the strength that (Joshua) showed to even be here tonight, and the strength that he had to show in that fight.” Hearn said that as the first round unfolded, he feared Joshua had come back too soon after the traumatic loss of his friends. But a beaming Joshua was bullish on the future. “I can’t be stopped,” he said. “I’m not going to be stopped. I’m not going to be denied.” The post Joshua survives knockdowns, stops Prenga appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Government urged to establish community autism units
items.description: Government has been urged to establish autism units in communities to support persons on the spectrum and ease the burden on families. Mr Abeiku Grant, Head of Programmes at the Autism Awareness Care and Training Centre (AACTC), made the call during an interview with the Ghana News Agency at the Centre’s annual arts and crafts exhibition in Haatso. He said the limited number of care centres meant parents and caregivers often travelled long distances with their children, an expense many struggling families could not afford. “Because of the level of care these children need, some parents are unable to work,” he stated. Mr Grant, who has worked with autistic children for 19 years, defined autism as a restricted pattern of behaviour. He noted that the situation was more challenging in rural areas where no dedicated centres existed. Mr Grant cautioned that children kept in isolation may struggle to function independently, stressing the need for exposure and training. He encouraged parents not to withdraw from society due to stigma but to seek support from experienced caregivers and professionals. Mr Grant recommended targeted government interventions to support parents and caregivers of autistic children. Mr Joseph Larmie, Coordinator at the Centre, said autism must not be seen as a limitation. “Just because somebody is autistic doesn’t mean the person cannot thrive. It all depends on the opportunity you give them,” he stated. Mr Larmie cited global figures such as Albert Einstein, Isaac Newton, Mozart and Elon Musk, widely believed to have been on the autism spectrum, as examples of what was possible with the right environment. “These people we think are very special… were also on the autism spectrum. And why did they thrive? It is because they were given the opportunity,” he added. The Centre, established 28 years ago, currently trains 22 learners daily and runs awareness campaigns and workshops for parents and teachers to equip them with skills to support autistic children. Items on display at the exhibition included crafts, paintings and vocational works produced by the learners.

items.title: Mahama leads Ghanaians to mark 14th Anniversary of Prof Mills’ passing
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama on Friday led Ghanaians to commemorate the 14th anniversary of the passing of President Professor John Evans Atta Mills with the laying of wreaths at his tomb at the Asomdwe (Peace) Park in Accra. President Mahama said the greatest tribute Ghanaians could pay to the late President was their commitment to the principles he cherished and exemplified, including integrity in public life, respect for democratic institutions, tolerance of differing views, compassion for the vulnerable, and an unwavering belief that Ghana’s progress must benefit all citizens. He noted that the late President’s vision of a peaceful, just and prosperous Ghana remained a work in progress. “I pledge to the memory of President John Evans Atta Mills that I shall continue to walk in the footsteps he left behind,” President Mahama stated. The President said Prof Mills’ dream now belonged to all Ghanaians and called on citizens to work together towards its fulfilment. He also expressed appreciation to Mrs Ernestina Naadu Mills, former First Lady, and the Mills family for sharing with the nation a man whose life continued to illuminate Ghana’s path. President Mahama said the annual gathering at Asomdwe Park was not merely to lay wreaths but to renew gratitude for a life that enriched and strengthened the nation. He observed that while time softens grief and pain, it also sharpens memory. “Fourteen years after Professor John Evans Atta Mills left us, I find that what endures most after his departure is not merely the memory of a President, but the memory of a man, a gentle soul whose character was his greatest strength,” the President said. He noted that some leaders command attention by the force of their personalities, and that President Mills commanded respect through the strength of his character and his values. He said the late President Mills believed that kindness was not a weakness, humility was not timidity, and decency was not incompatible with effective leadership. President Mahama said the late President Mills demonstrated that one could occupy the highest office of the land without losing one’s humanity. “I had the rare privilege of serving by his side. Beyond Cabinet meetings, official engagements and the weighty affairs of state, I came to know a leader who listened more than he spoke, who reflected before he acted, and who never allowed the burdens of office to diminish his compassion for the ordinary people he served,” he said. President Mahama described the late leader as a statesman who commanded respect through the strength of his character and values rather than through force of personality. According to him, Prof Mills believed that kindness was not weakness, humility was not timidity and decency was fully compatible with effective leadership. He noted that the late President demonstrated that one could occupy the highest office in the land without losing one’s humanity. He said Prof Mills’ leadership was anchored in conscience and reminded Ghanaians that history ultimately judges leaders by the depth of their convictions and the impact of their service rather than by the bitterness of political contests. “That is why his legacy continues to resonate. He taught us that public office is not a prize to be claimed, but a trust given by the people to be honoured.” President Mahama added that the late President understood that leadership was most effective when it sought to unite rather than divide, heal rather than injure, and inspire rather than intimidate. He said Prof Mills’ quiet wisdom and steady temperament continued to guide him in discharging the responsibilities entrusted to him by Ghanaians. The President expressed the hope that future generations who never had the opportunity to know Prof Mills would come to appreciate that true greatness is often quiet, genuine strength is often humble and enduring leadership is measured by service rather than acclaim. The commemoration, organised by the National Democratic Congress in collaboration with the J.E.A. Mills Memorial Heritage, was attended by Mr Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, Speaker of Parliament, Ministers of State, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries.

items.title: Tuggar Campaign Organisation denies defections, condemns alleged misinformation
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Tuggar Campaign Organisation has dismissed claims that supporters of the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Yusuf Maitama Tuggar, have defected to another governorship aspirant, describing the reports as false and misleading. In a statement issued on Saturday, the organisation said the claims, made during a recent press conference by supporters of another aspirant, were intended to create a false impression of shifting political support within the All Progressives Congress (APC). The campaign maintained that no member or group within its structure had been authorised to negotiate or declare support for any other aspirant on behalf of Ambassador Tuggar. According to the organisation, the campaign remains united and committed to supporting Tuggar’s political aspiration. It also urged political actors and their supporters to conduct their campaigns responsibly and avoid the spread of unverified information capable of misleading party members and the public. The organisation further called for issue-based campaigns, stressing the need for honesty, integrity and respect for democratic principles throughout the political process. items.title: Confusion, protests trail allocation of shops at newly commissioned Modibbo Adama Ultra-Modern Market
items.description: By Umar Yusuf, Yola The Adamawa State Government has blamed leaders of traders’ unions for the confusion and protests that have trailed the allocation of shops at the newly commissioned Modibbo Adama Ultra-Modern Market in Yola. The government alleged that irregularities and other sharp practices occurred during the compilation of the list of beneficiaries who owned shops before the market was demolished and reconstructed. The Commissioner for Commerce and Industry, Chief Joab Sahma, told journalists in Yola that the ministry had received numerous complaints from individuals and groups who claimed they were genuine former shop owners but were excluded from the allocation process. According to him, the government constituted a committee to investigate the complaints and review the lists submitted by the various market unions. “The committee discovered several irregularities allegedly perpetrated during the compilation of the lists by some union leaders. It found that fictitious names had been inserted, while genuine former shop owners were omitted,” he said. Sahma said the government had no option but to remove the fictitious names to ensure that only legitimate beneficiaries were allocated shops. He further alleged that some union leaders manipulated the process for personal gain, stressing that the government would not condone such practices. The commissioner also alleged that some unscrupulous individuals exploited the desperation of prospective shop owners by collecting millions of naira from them under the guise of securing allocations. He assured genuine former shop owners that they would receive their allocations after the verification process was completed. Sahma also disclosed that the shopping complex currently under construction, which is about 80 per cent completed, is expected to be handed over to the state government on or before September. He added that the Jimeta Modern Market would also be renovated as part of the government’s efforts to improve commercial activities and boost trade in the state. items.title: Situationer: Resorting to ‘encounters’: are Sindh police losing faith in legal system?
items.description: WHILE the killing of suspected criminals in alleged encounters is not a new phenomenon, it is rare in Karachi for arrested suspects to be brought to raids to arrest their accomplices and for them to end up dead “by firing from their own accomplices”. Thursday’s killing of three suspects, who were arrested recently for murdering a doctor during a robbery in Clifton, in a “shoot-out” between police and their alleged accomplices gives rise to the impression that Sindh police are now gradually moving towards the Punjab Crime Control Department’s (CCD) style of “dispensing justice”, which has been quite infamous for such encounters. Dawn reached out to several top officials for comments, but they declined to go on record. However, in background conversations, they said this was partly due to “frustration with the criminal justice system” and partly to prevent “the entry of criminals from Punjab” into Sindh, particularly Karachi. They said several suspects had fled the CCD operations in Lahore and came to Karachi, where they were committing heinous crimes. They said that the police have adopted a “zero tolerance” policy against crime and criminals as proclaimed offenders and habitual criminals usually get bail and return to the streets to resume committing crimes. As Punjab police are widely associated with alleged killings of held suspects, recent incidents in Karachi point to where Sindh police are taking their lead from Besides, the officials said that it had been noticed that several criminals had fled Punjab and had come to Karachi because of perceived proactive policing in Punjab and had started committing crimes in the city. In order to deter criminals of Punjab from taking shelter in Karachi, pro-active policing has been enhanced, the sources said. Citing such cases, they said that recently a suspect had been arrested in the city who was wanted in 140 cases in different parts of Punjab. Similarly, a gang from Punjab had been busted in Karachi after they had looted Rs6.5 million in Saddar. Moreover, criminals had demanded protection money from a famous sweet shop in Ittehad Town and also carried out firing on the shop for extortion. It transpired during the investigation that this gang of criminals belonged to Rawalpindi. They had come to Karachi to carry out crimes after running away from actions of the CCD in Punjab. “We are moving towards a hard state by bringing changes to police’s attitudes and policies to take forcible action against crime and criminals,” observed South DIG Syed Asad Raza, without elaborating. Another senior official said, “encounters” make a “difference” as a particular type of criminals were involved in violent crimes and these crimes could only be controlled through “elimination” of such hardened criminals. ‘Risk of collateral damage’ However, the official warned that there is always a risk of “collateral damage” as recently happened in Chakwal in Punjab where the CCD action against criminals led to killing of an innocent girl. However, an official of the Citizens Police Liaison Committee (CPLC), who wished not to be named, said that a long-lasting solution lies in “improving criminal justice system”. He said that recently the CPLC and the police jointly arrested two suspected extortionists red-handed when they were extracting Rs1 million protection money from a trader. The CPLC officials were thinking to issue a press release to the media as the arrest was not properly covered by the media, but to their utter surprise, they came to know that both the accused had already been released on bail. The CPLC official added that it should be investigated by the authorities whether it was a “faulty investigation” by investigators that helped the extortionists get bail. Otherwise, the authorities concerned should take up this issue with the chief justice of Sindh High Court. CCD’s massive apparatus A senior police official from Punjab told Dawn that the CCD is part of Punjab police and is not alone in controlling crime. “There are other factors as well that have contributed to crime control efforts in the province.” The official added that the introduction of technology, safe cities project, provision of modern gadgets, establishment of a “state-of-the-art” forensic lab, crime scene units equipped with “European-like” vehicles for collecting evidence, fingerprinting, DNA testing, etc, were among the factors whose combined impact had contributed to reducing crime by 80 per cent in Punjab. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Flooding: Nasarawa desilts drainages, arrests 126 sanitation defaulters
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has intensified environmental sanitation monitoring across the state as the peak of the rainy season sets in, in a bid to prevent flooding. The government also disclosed that no fewer than 126 people were arrested during the July monthly environmental sanitation exercise for violating the state’s sanitation laws. The Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources, Dr. Margaret Elayo, disclosed this while briefing journalists on Saturday in Lafia after the sanitation exercise. Represented by the Permanent Secretary in the ministry, Mr. Ede Yakubu, the commissioner described the exercise as highly successful, citing widespread public participation. Elayo attributed the success to a new enforcement strategy that involved setting up surprise roadblocks at strategic locations across the state. “Today’s exercise was very effective because many defaulters were apprehended and prosecuted. People came out in large numbers to participate in the sanitation exercise. “We had never mounted a roadblock near the College of Agriculture before, but we changed our strategy today and caught many violators by surprise. I personally led the team to monitor those entering and leaving the town, and that made the exercise more effective,” she said. Speaking on measures to tackle flooding during the rainy season, Elayo said the Nasarawa State Waste Management Agency and the Nasarawa State Environmental Protection Agency would deploy personnel for daily monitoring, waste evacuation and public sensitisation against indiscriminate dumping of refuse in drainage channels. “Once the drainages are cleared to allow the free flow of water, flooding is greatly reduced. That is why we are moving from monthly sanitation monitoring to daily surveillance to ensure a cleaner environment,” she added. Also speaking, the Chief Prosecuting Officer, Abubakar Mohammed, confirmed that 126 offenders were arrested across the state during the exercise, with commercial tricycle (Keke) operators accounting for the majority. He, however, noted that compliance with the sanitation exercise was generally high, as most shops remained closed during the exercise, while other individuals found moving during the restricted sanitation hours were also arrested. Mohammed further disclosed that enforcement of drainage desilting had been strengthened in line with Section 13 of the state’s environmental law, which requires property owners to clear drainages in front of their premises. “Last week alone, we arrested 16 people for violating the drainage clearance directive. If you go around town now, you will see residents clearing refuse to keep the environment clean and ensure the free flow of water,” he said. He added that while the monthly environmental sanitation exercise would continue, it would now be complemented by daily waste evacuation and public sensitisation throughout the rainy season. items.title: Police urge peaceful Homowo celebration, warn against violence
items.description: The Tema Regional Police Command has appealed to residents to celebrate this year’s Homowo Festival peacefully and refrain from acts that could disrupt public order. Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Eric Asamoah Asiedu, Tema Regional Police Commander, said the festival period would witness traditional rulers, priests and priestesses performing customary rites before, during and after the celebrations, including the sprinkling of kpokpoi, the traditional Homowo meal. DCOP Asiedu noted that disputes over who had the authority to perform the sprinkling of kpokpoi had, in previous years, led to confrontations, violence and breaches of the peace. He, therefore, urged residents to celebrate the festival in an atmosphere of peace, unity and mutual respect while adhering to the laws of the country. The Regional Commander cautioned celebrants against engaging in violence, unnecessary confrontations, disorderly conduct and other acts capable of endangering public safety. He assured the public that the Police would provide adequate security throughout the festival period and deal decisively with individuals who engaged in criminal activities under the guise of the celebrations. DCOP Asiedu also expressed concern over growing tensions arising from chieftaincy disputes in some traditional areas. He urged all factions, supporters and interested parties to avoid acts of provocation, violence, unlawful assembly and the use of vigilante groups. The Regional Commander said chieftaincy disputes should be resolved through the appropriate legal and traditional mechanisms, warning that anyone whose actions threatened public peace would be arrested and prosecuted. DCOP Asiedu further warned armed robbers, drug traffickers and other criminal elements operating within the Tema region that the Police had intensified intelligence gathering, patrols and collaboration with other security agencies to combat crime. He stressed that there would be no safe haven for criminals in the region and reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property.

items.title: ‘I’ve never endorsed Peter Obi or any politician’
items.description: … Falz sets the record straight By Tony-Okafor Favour Rapper and actor Folarin Falana, popularly known as Falz, has debunked claims that he endorsed Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi or any other politician during the 2023 general elections. Speaking on ARISE News Prime Time during the week, the award-winning artiste clarified that while he was vocal about civic participation, he never publicly backed any candidate or party. “Just a point of correction: I’ve never, in 2023 or at any point, openly supported any politician or political party,” Falz said. “I’ve only actively encouraged people to go out to vote and let their intentions be known. What I clamour for is a free and fair democratic process.” Falz said his decision to stay neutral comes from his frustration with Nigeria’s political cycle, where the same set of leaders keep returning to power. “We’ve been going in cycles, and it just seems like almost the same crop of people we keep on reshuffling. At the end of the day, it’s tough to even sit anywhere and vouch for a Nigerian politician in 2026,” he stated. However, the singer added that he may consider an endorsement in the future if he finds a candidate he truly believes in. “If I see someone that I feel 100 per cent is the one, maybe I would. But as it stands, I’m just trying to be cautious,” he added. Falz also urged Nigerians, especially young people, to come out massively in the 2027 general elections. According to him, higher voter turnout will make it harder to manipulate results and will strengthen democracy. The post ‘I’ve never endorsed Peter Obi or any politician’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Troops rescue five family members as search intensifies for abducted Zamfara LG chairman
items.description: ….Two Policemen, Vigilante, Civilian Killed By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation to secure the release of the Executive Chairman of Bungudu Local Government Area of Zamfara State, Hon. Nura Umar Abdullahi, who was abducted by suspected terrorists. In a statement issued on Saturday, the Joint Task Force (North West) said the attackers stormed the chairman’s residence in the early hours of July 25, 2026, overpowering police officers and vigilante personnel on guard before abducting him and several members of his family. The statement said troops responded immediately after hearing gunfire and engaged the fleeing attackers in a fierce gun battle. According to the military, the swift response forced the attackers to abandon five members of the chairman’s family, including his wife, mother, two children and another relative, all of whom were rescued unharmed. The attackers, however, escaped into nearby bushes with the council chairman. The incident claimed the lives of two police officers, a local vigilante and a civilian. The military said the slain security personnel fought gallantly while resisting the attackers. The chairman’s elder brother, Alhaji Bello Umar, also sustained injuries during the attack. Following the incident, the Theatre Command said it activated a joint rescue operation involving troops of Operation Fansan Yamma, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and local vigilantes. Security personnel, it added, are conducting targeted operations in areas believed to be the terrorists’ hideouts in an effort to rescue the abducted chairman safely. The command said it has deployed all available resources and is working closely with other security agencies to ensure the success of the operation. It assured the Zamfara State Government and residents that every lawful operational measure is being taken to secure the chairman’s release and bring those responsible for the attack to justice. The military also urged members of the public to remain calm, go about their lawful activities and provide credible information through established security channels to support the ongoing rescue efforts. items.title: NDC insists government appointees must resign before contesting party executive elections
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has reaffirmed that government appointees who fail to resign from their positions will not be eligible to contest the party’s upcoming executive elections. The party says its long-standing directive requiring government appointees to step down before seeking elective positions within the NDC remains in force and will be strictly enforced throughout the electoral process. According to the party, only individuals who are no longer serving in government positions will qualify to file nominations and participate in the internal elections. The NDC also indicated that, although reports have emerged suggesting that some appointees have resigned, the party headquarters has yet to receive formal notifications from most of those individuals. It explained that the official status of prospective candidates would be determined during the nomination, filing and vetting process, when evidence of resignation and eligibility would be verified. The party, however, confirmed that some officials, including the Eastern Regional Chairman, the Eastern Regional Communications Officer and Leland Tay, who is contesting for the National Chairman position, have resigned from their respective roles. The directive is expected to affect a number of government officials who may be considering contesting for executive positions while still holding public appointments, with the party also ruling out any special exemptions from the resignation requirement. Speaking on Citi FM on Saturday, July 25, 2026, the NDC’s Acting IT Director, Jibril Mahdi, said government appointees who remain in office would automatically be disqualified from contesting the elections. “Whoever is in office is not qualified to contest our elections,” he said. Mr Mahdi added that the party headquarters had not officially received resignation notices from most of the individuals reported to have stepped down. “Officially, we have not received any notice from anybody that has resigned. Whatever we are hearing is based on the social media information because, at party headquarters, we are not the appointing authority,” he said. He further stressed that the party had not received any requests for exemptions, insisting: “For now, whoever is still in office is automatically ineligible to contest as it stands.” The NDC is expected to continue its internal electoral calendar following the completion of branch-level elections, with preparations underway for the next phase of the party’s executive elections.

items.title: ENUGU AIR: How crew’s skill, rain averted major incident – CEO
items.description: By Dickson Omobola The management of Enugu State-owned carrier, Enugu Air, has said the professionalism of its flight crew and favourable weather conditions contributed to the safe outcome of the airline’s recent runway excursion. An Enugu Air Flight 4264, with registration number 5N-ENR, from Lagos to Benin, the Edo State capital, suffered a runway excursion on Thursday. All 63 passengers and five crew members on board were safely evacuated. Chief Executive Officer and Accountable Manager of the airline, Captain Tolu Ita, while reacting to the development, said the pilots handled the situation expertly, adding that the wet conditions and grassy terrain might have prevented the incident from escalating into a serious issue. Speaking on TVC News last night, Ita disclosed that, based on the accounts of the flight crew, the aircraft landed on the runway and deployed its brakes and reverse thrust but failed to stop before overrunning the runway. She, however, urged travellers not to stop flying the airline, saying a single incident could not define Enugu Air’s safety record, as it had successfully completed more than 3,500 flights. Her words: “From our perspective, especially because we are required as an airline to carry out an internal investigation, which we have done, and we have to submit our report also, what happened is, it was a normal flight. Based on several recounts, the crew landed. “It was a normal profile, landed on the runway and deployed brakes and reverse thrust but the plane did not stop. Of course, they ended up exiting the whole runway and ended up in the bush. After stopping, they carried out a normal emergency evacuation. “They had to use emergency slides to come out of the aircraft because there were no slides. But this is something they did impromptu because they are always prepared. As I said, we have cooperated with all regulations. Our engineers are currently working with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, NSIB, to try and get the popular black box because the black box will record everything. “So, which is why we keep emphasising that until that is done by the NSIB, we can’t make any official reports. But, we have to do our own preliminary investigation and reports, which is part of what will be submitted and the NSIB would also consider. “Since we got our Air Operator’s Certificate, AOC, on March 10 and we started operation as Enugu Air on March 16, we have done and successfully completed over 3,500 flights. One flight out of 3,500 flights is not enough to define an airline. “By the way, there are very leading airlines in this country that have had not one, but several excursions. It does not necessarily have dent safety records. Aviation is an ecosystem, and every successful flight means every ecosystem, the support, government, the facilities have done their job. “So, one in many is not enough to define an airline. I can tell you, I can beat my chest that Enugu Air is a safe airline in the country to fly right now in Nigeria. First, I would like to recognise the hand of God in that (incident), because a lot of things could have happened. Let me not talk on the technicalities of what happened that the two main landing gears collapsed. And one of them even actually collapsed into the wing carrying fuel. Those wings had fuel in them. “Yes, pilot technique, the pilots were amazing. But I could also say the fact that it was raining probably helped. And then the grass prevented sparks. Because what you need is just a spark. But the fact that the surface was not hard, that smoothness on the grass kind of tempered it. That is my opinion, by the way.” The post ENUGU AIR: How crew’s skill, rain averted major incident – CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US holds fire against Iran as reports emerge of stockpile concerns
items.description: Iran passed another night without US airstrikes on Sunday, as Washington paused a war nearing its fifth month and reports emerged that concerns over dwindling munitions were restraining plans for further escalation. The lull has revived hopes of a return to negotiations after nearly two weeks of consecutive nightly US bombardments, although US media reported the pause could also reflect pressure on stockpiles of Patriot interceptors and other defensive weapons. Fighting over the strategic Strait of Hormuz derailed diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran, but the conflict then expanded beyond the vital energy corridor to include attacks on US bases, regional shipping and Gulf allies. However, US operations against Iran were “on a hold”, CNN reported, quoting an unidentified Pentagon source, even as US President Donald Trump threatened a “much higher level” of strikes on Friday. Plans to escalate the campaign have been shelved in part because of those shrinking supplies, The New York Times reported, citing two people briefed on the matter. Trump also faces the risk of a wider Middle East war, the estrangement of vulnerable Gulf allies and further shocks to the global economy, the newspaper said. Vice President JD Vance and top US general Dan Caine both raised concerns about escalation at a White House meeting on Friday, CNN reported. Caine told Trump the military could carry out the options available to him successfully but warned of the possible implications, according to the network. – ‘Much higher level’ – Trump said on Friday he had not decided whether to return to an all-out operation. “We’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious,” he told journalists. Trump said Iran faced a choice between a deal and strikes at a “much higher level”. The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial US midterm elections in November. The Pentagon had presented Trump with a plan for a 14th night of strikes but he declined to authorise it in favour of a push for talks, Axios reported. – New front – Fighting has meanwhile spread to a new front. Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they struck Saudi Aramco sites in Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday, a day after Riyadh bombed Houthi targets. A surface-to-air battery operated by Greek personnel in Saudi Arabia downed two ballistic missiles and a drone over Yanbu, the Greek air force media office said. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had stopped four ships attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz in 24 hours. Tehran’s effective blockade of the waterway remains the central flashpoint with Washington. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran could not be blamed for the escalation and offered to broker talks between the Houthis and Riyadh, saying “there is no military solution”. items.title: Osun Election: AYIWOLA APC youths hold vote sensitization rally for Oyebamiji
items.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo Youths from the three local government areas of Iwo Federal Constituency on Saturday staged a vote sensitization in support of the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Osun State, Mr Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO), declaring their commitment to delivering the constituency for the party during the August 15 governorship election. The rally, which attracted thousands of the APC Youth in the onstituency, drew participants from Iwo, Ayedire and Olaoluwa local government areas. The procession moved through major parts of Iwo, including LA Grammar School, Oke Ibode, Idi Agbede, Ojude Oba, Oke Ode, Olu Ponona and parts of Ayedire Local Government Area, with supporters chanting campaign slogans and displaying party flags. Speaking during the rally, the APC candidate for the Osun State House of Assembly, Olaoluwa State Constituency, Hon. Adegbile Abefe, said the turnout demonstrated the confidence of youths in Oyebamiji’s leadership. According to him, the youths gathered to showcase their strength and support for the APC governorship candidate, whom they described as a capable and competent leader to govern Osun State. Abefe also criticised Governor Ademola Adeleke’s administration, alleging that it had failed to fulfil campaign promises on security, healthcare and road infrastructure. “We want to prove to the whole world that the youths of Iwo Federal Constituency have rejected the incumbent governor because of what we described as his failed promises. The crowd here today shows the organic love and support the people have for Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji,” he said. Also addressing the gathering, the Chairman of Youth Mobilisation in Iwo Federal Constituency, Comrade Muyideen Abdulgafar, expressed confidence that the APC would secure victory across the constituency in the governorship poll. He alleged that the current administration had failed to provide quality infrastructure and adequate security, adding that Oyebamiji possessed the competence and capacity to address the state’s challenges if elected. “We are very sure that by August 15, we are going to deliver Iwo Federal Constituency for the APC. Our governorship candidate has what it takes to move Osun State to greater heights,” Abdulgafar said. A member of the APC Campaign Council, Yakub Atanda, described the rally as only “a tip of the iceberg,” claiming that about 10,000 youths participated in the mobilisation exercise. He said the massive turnout reflected the level of support enjoyed by the APC candidate ahead of the election. items.title: MQM-P steps up campaign for creation of new provinces
items.description: • In Hyderabad rally, Khalid Maqbool says his party has not rowed back on its demand for separate province to be carved out from Sindh • Existing administrative system has failed to address governance needs of growing population, Kamal tells press conference in Karachi HYDERABAD / KARACHI: The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) intensified its campaign for the creation of new provinces on Saturday, as party chairman Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui led a rally in Hyderabad, while senior leader Mustafa Kamal held a press conference in Karachi to reiterate their demand for new administrative units across the country, including Sindh. The party argued that the existing administrative structure has failed to meet the governance and development needs of the country’s growing population, particularly in Sindh, and maintains that establishing new provinces is essential to ensuring better service delivery, equitable resource distribution and effective governance. However, two separate events highlighted increasing internal rifts as Mr Kamal did not attend the Hyderabad rally, while Dr Siddiqui was absent from the press conference held at the party’s temporary headquarters in Bahadurabad. ‘Power show’ in Hyderabad In Hyderabad, the MQM-P staged a rally from Liberty Chowk to Kohinoor Chowk. Addressing the participants, party chairman Dr Siddiqui said that the MQM had not withdrawn its demand for a separate province to be carved out from Sindh and told critics that the province would be created on the basis of “exchange of land” and “mother tongue”. He said that Mohajirs from India had arrived here by choice, not by chance. He said it was under the Liaquat-Nehru pact that such migration had taken place. He said that former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto had decided on urban and rural Sindh, and it was also decided that if the chief minister was a Sindhi-speaking fellow, then the governor would be an Urdu-speaking individual to be nominated by the party that had the mandate of urban Sindh. He said that 97 per cent of the Sindh budget was provided by Karachi and the rest came from other major cities like Hyderabad and Mirpurkhas. He said two classes existed in Sindh — one was nurturing Sindh with 100pctaxes, while the other was enjoying it with zero contribution. “If we are counted fairly, then the demand for a separate province will be raised from the other side,” he said. He said the MQM-P had not withdrawn its separate province demand, and those who questioned where this province would be should understand it would be created on the basis of ‘mother tongue Sindh’ and ‘exchanged land’. New provinces’ demand not based on ethnic lines: Kamal Mustafa Kamal speaks at the presser.—Dawn Earlier, senior MQM-P leader and Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal told a press conference in Karachi that the establishment of new provinces on administrative grounds had become essential to ensuring better governance, efficient public service delivery and balanced development. He said the demand for new provinces was not based on ethnic or linguistic considerations but on administrative necessity. The increasing population and expanding urban centres, he said, required a governance structure that could effectively respond to people’s needs. Mr Kamal claimed that the Sindh government had received Rs22 trillion over the past 18 years but allocated only Rs680 billion to Karachi, despite the city contributing more than 90pc of the province’s revenue. He said that if the pre-2010 formula for sharing General Sales Tax (GST) revenues had remained in place, Karachi would have received around Rs2 trillion, which could have been invested in improving roads, water supply, public transport, schools, hospitals and employment opportunities. He accused the Sindh government of centralising powers after the 18th Amendment while failing to provide basic services such as clean drinking water, sanitation, education and healthcare in Karachi and other parts of the province. He alleged that despite the devolution of powers under the 18th Amendment, local governments had remained financially and administratively weak, leaving citizens deprived of effective municipal services. He maintained that local bodies should be empowered to resolve civic issues at the grassroots level. The MQM-P leader said his party had proposed constitutional amendments in parliament aimed at improving governance and strengthening local government institutions but alleged that the PPP used its parliamentary majority to block those proposals. He added that the party would now take its campaign for public rights to the streets after failing to secure legislative support. He urged citizens to participate in the party’s planned protest rally in Shah Faisal Town on Sunday (today) and raise their voices for improved governance, transparency and equitable distribution of resources. Responding to questions from journalists, Mr Kamal said the party would continue pursuing democratic and constitutional means to press its demands while expanding public awareness about its proposals for administrative reforms. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Les Lionnes démarrent le tournoi face à l’Algérie, ce dimanche
items.description: L’édition 2026 de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (Can) féminine démarre ce dimanche 26 juillet, à Rabat, au Maroc. En ouverture de la compétition, les Lionnes du Sénégal rencontrent l’Algérie à partir de 17 heures. Pour une 4e participation au tournoi, le Sénégal vise les demi-finales. Le coup d’envoi de la 14e édition de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (Can) féminine sera donné, ce dimanche 26 juillet, au Stade olympique de Rabat. En ouverture du tournoi, le Sénégal rencontre l’Algérie à 17 heures pour bien démarrer sa campagne. En terre marocaine, les Lionnes ambitionnent de franchir un nouveau palier, après deux qualifications en quart de finale. Comme annoncé par le sélectionneur national, Mame Moussa Cissé, le Sénégal vise une place dans le top 4 continental. Une progression qui devrait permettre à l’équipe de valider par la même occasion, sa présence à la prochaine Coupe du monde de la catégorie prévue en 2027 au Brésil. Mais le technicien veut déjà bien démarrer le tournoi face à la formation algérienne. « Le premier match est extrêmement important. Nous sommes tous focalisés sur l’Algérie. Il nous faut faire un bon résultat sur ce match », disait-il, lundi dernier, lors de la cérémonie de remise du drapeau national, au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor. Il ajoutait par la même occasion : « L’Algérie est une grande équipe qui a aussi envie de faire la même chose que nous. Elle était quart de finaliste comme nous lors de l’édition précédente. Donc, cela ne va pas être une chose facile des deux côtés ». Quarts de finalistes de la dernière édition qui avait déjà lieu au Maroc, les Lionnes vont évoluer dans le groupe A, aux côtés donc de l’Algérie, du pays hôte et du Kenya. Dans la deuxième rencontre du jour, les deux dernières équipes vont en découdre à 20 heures, avant la suite de la compétition, lundi. Ousseynou POUYE

items.title: Osun NURTW: Oyewale group resumes office, says crisis is over
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The newly inaugurated Caretaker Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Osun State Council, Alhaji Kazeem Oyewale, popularly known as Ashiri Eniba, has assured residents that peace has returned to motor parks across the state, announcing the resumption of union activities following the resolution of its leadership crisis. The state council had been embroiled in a leadership dispute between the Oyewale faction and the faction led by Nurudeen Wakili, popularly known as Alowonle. The crisis resulted in protests, violence, disruption of commercial activities and the suspension of union operations in motor parks by local government chairmen across the state. The council chairmen subsequently announced Oyewale’s appointment as caretaker chairman, and he was later inaugurated by the national leadership of the union despite the Osun State Government’s opposition to the move. Speaking after assuming office on Saturday, Oyewale said the newly constituted state executive members were recently invited to Abuja, where they were inaugurated to oversee the affairs of the Osun State Council. He appealed to residents not to associate members of the union with violence, describing commercial drivers as law-abiding citizens committed to their livelihoods. Oyewale also urged the police to conclude investigations into the killings of some union members during the crisis and called on members who had stayed away to return to the union. According to him, “Leadership changes are normal in every organisation. That is why we were invited to Abuja for our inauguration to officially take charge of the affairs of the Osun State Council. “I want to assure the people of Osun State that commercial drivers are not hoodlums. We are responsible family men. The police are investigating the killings recorded during the crisis, and we hope justice will be served. “Our doors remain open to every member because we are one family. I appeal to those who have stayed away to return to the union. I also urge the Osun State Government to work with us. We are ready to cooperate with all stakeholders because we are an independent union. “I want to assure residents that peace has returned to our motor parks and all issues have been resolved. I also commend the Nigeria Police Force for its role in restoring peace and encourage the officers to remain committed to maintaining security. Commercial activities will fully resume across our garages on Monday.” Also speaking, the union’s Interim Secretary and Group 2 Chairman for Ife Federal Constituency, Ayinde Mutiu, said normal activities had resumed across motor parks following the resolution of the leadership dispute. He appealed to members to embrace peace and avoid actions capable of disrupting public order, stressing that the NURTW remains one united family despite the recent challenges. items.title: La Sonatel franchit la barre des 1 000 milliards de FCfa de chiffre d’affaires
items.description: Le Groupe Sonatel a réalisé un chiffre d’affaires consolidé de 1 049,8 milliards de FCfa au terme du premier semestre 2026, en progression de 9,3 % par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente. Cette performance est portée par la forte croissance des activités Data, du Très Haut Débit fixe et d’Orange Money, confirme la solidité du modèle économique de l’opérateur présent au Sénégal, au Mali, en Guinée, en Guinée-Bissau et en Sierra Leone. Pour soutenir cette dynamique, Sonatel a consacré 154 milliards de FCfa à ses investissements, soit 15 % de son chiffre d’affaires, principalement pour accélérer le déploiement du Très Haut Débit fixe et mobile. Commentant ces résultats, le directeur général du Groupe Sonatel, Brelotte Bâ, a souligné que « les résultats de ce premier semestre démontrent que les investissements engagés dans le déploiement de la Fibre et du Très Haut Débit produisent des résultats concrets », réaffirmant l’ambition du groupe de demeurer le partenaire de référence de la transformation numérique en Afrique de l’Ouest.
