items.title: End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists in Yemen
items.description: Click to expand Image Muhammad Aidha’s car in the yard of a police station, where it had been moved to after an explosive device planted in the car detonated and killed him, in Mukalla, Yemen, June 25, 2026. © 2026 Reuters Journalist Muhammad Aidha, who had reported for the Saudi-owned Al Arabiya and Al Hadath channels since 2019, was killed in Mukalla in eastern Yemen on June 24 by an explosive device planted in his car. Three days later, on June 27, Marib security forces detained journalist Hamoud Haza while he was covering a public event. Haza told Human Rights Watch that he was held incommunicado and released two days later, only after he signed a pledge to not criticize the internationally recognized government and its minister of information. The Yemeni Journalists Syndicate condemned Aidha’s killing, saying the attack “added to a series of crimes and violations against journalists and media workers, including the assassination of journalists Rasha al-Harazi and Saber al-Haidari in Aden.” The National Organization of Yemeni Reporters said in a statement that over 90 journalists and media workers have been killed since Yemen’s conflict began in 2015, adding, “This bloody toll reflects the desire of the parties to the conflict to impose a complete media blackout and to entrench a culture of impunity.” Government authorities are not alone in their abuses against journalists. In March, Houthi forces abducted journalist Salah al-Deen al-Rawhani from his home in Sanaa, and he has not been heard from since, according to the International Federation of Journalists. In September 2025, Human Rights Watch documented warring parties’ systematic violations against Yemeni journalists, including killings, enforced disappearances, torture, and other ill-treatment. The report found all parties to the conflict, including the Houthis, the Southern Transitional Council, and the Yemeni government, have committed serious abuses with impunity against journalists and media workers. International humanitarian law obligates all warring parties to protect civilians, including journalists, who are not taking a direct part in hostilities. International human rights law further protects journalists’ rights to liberty, security of person, and freedom of expression, and prohibits arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. The Yemeni government should conduct a prompt, impartial, and transparent investigation into the killing of Mohammed Aydah, and investigate all other attacks on journalists that have taken place within territories under their control, and hold those responsible to account. Houthi authorities should also release all detained journalists and media workers, including Salah al-Deen al-Rawhani.

items.title: Quid pro quo
items.description: MERE hours after the US signed a landmark civil nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, American President Donald Trump sprang a surprise : the deal would only go through if the Saudis recognised Israel and signed the so-called Abraham Accords. While Riyadh has remained silent over the demand, media reports indicate that recognition of the Zionist state was not part of the negotiations, and is most likely a Trumpian addition to the deal. Saudi Arabia must join “the very respected and successful Abraham Accords”, Mr Trump said, championing his pet project dating back to his first term, when the UAE, Bahrain and Morocco officially recognised Israel. To ensure there was no ambiguity about Mr Trump’s announcement, the White House press secretary said “the deal is off” if the Saudis refused to join the Accords. The American leader has been pressing Saudi Arabia and other Muslim states, including Pakistan, for some time to recognise Israel. However, this remains a morally reprehensible proposition considering Tel Aviv’s genocidal violence in Gaza, and its refusal to accept the idea of an independent Palestinian state. Accepting Israel would mean legitimising its violence against the Palestinians, as well as its neighbouring Arab states and Iran. The official Saudi position remains that recognition cannot come unless there is a ‘pathway’ to a Palestinian state. Pakistan too — which has resisted earlier American calls to embrace Israel — has clearly stated that until there is a Palestinian state with pre-1967 borders and Al Quds as its capital, recognition is not on the agenda. Moreover, there is widespread support for Palestine amongst the public, and disgust with the atrocious levels of violence unleashed by Israel on the Palestinian people. This makes recognition highly improbable. As for Tel Aviv’s position, the current Israeli prime minister has said that a Palestinian state will not happen. Even more ‘liberal’ Israeli politicians are steadfast in their opposition to a Palestinian state. Mr Trump’s eagerness to bring the Saudis on board is understandable. While many OIC members have accepted Israel, due to Saudi Arabia’s role as the custodian of Islam’s holiest sites, its recognition would open the floodgates for wider normalisation with Israel in the Muslim world. Pakistan should remain wary. It must not change its principled position on the Palestine question, and resist all America’s attempts at coercing it to embrace the Zionist state. The Israel ‘brand’ has become toxic the world over, due to Tel Aviv’s extermination campaign in Gaza, and its aggression against Lebanon, Syria, Yemen and Iran. Should such a state be embraced by the Muslim world, when it shows zero remorse for its murderous policies, remains committed to resisting a Palestinian state, and when its leaders openly speak of desecrating Al Aqsa? Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Uncertainty in Gulf likely to keep policy rate unchanged
items.description: KARACHI: The State Bank is widely expected to keep its policy interest rate unchanged at its monetary policy meeting on Monday (July 27), as policymakers are unlikely to alter the benchmark rate amid heightened uncertainty following the Gulf war. Economists, researchers and analysts are still assessing the war’s impact on Pakistan, but there is broad agreement that it pushed global oil prices above $100 per barrel , affecting economies worldwide, including Pakistan. Analysts closely tracking the economy say it would be difficult to maintain macroeconomic stability with sluggish growth. They believe the State Bank is unlikely to risk undermining that stability by changing the policy rate. Despite the surge in global oil prices, which has intensified inflationary pressures, the government and the State Bank hope to keep average CPI inflation within the 7-8pc range in FY27. While some analysts question this outlook, most believe it will depend on developments in the region. The US strikes on Iran continued, while Iran also targeted American bases in several Gulf countries. Analysts say State Bank is prioritising stability over growth amid tensions The State Bank reduced its policy rate by 50 basis points to 10.5pc on Dec 15, 2025, but raised it by 100 basis points to 11.5pc on April 27. Since then, it has kept the rate unchanged despite persistent calls from the trade and industrial sectors for a cut of at least 200 basis points. The central bank has refrained from adopting a more pro-growth stance by lowering interest rates to encourage greater liquidity flows to the private sector. Banks, too, have remained reluctant to increase private-sector lending, preferring instead to invest in government securities. They invested Rs5.9 trillion in government papers during FY26, while the private sector — the engine of the economy — received only Rs1.4tr, mostly for short-term working capital. Analysts believe there is little chance of either a rate cut or an increase. While lower rates could fuel inflationary pressures, a hike would further dampen economic growth. The World Bank recently projected Pakistan’s economic growth at below 4pc in FY27, compared with the government’s target of more than 4pc. Surveys conducted by brokerage houses show that more than 90pc of stakeholders expect the State Bank to leave the policy rate unchanged, while only a small number foresee a modest increase. Financial experts say the course of the Gulf conflict — whether it escalates or de-escalates — will shape the outlook for many economies, including Pakistan, as elevated oil prices could derail growth in several developing countries. They believe the State Bank’s policy decision will largely depend on the evolving regional situation, making an unch­a­nged policy rate the most likely outcome. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Vicente Grimalt: “Vendo caprichos que no sabes que necesitas hasta que los ves”
items.description: El señor Vicent, así le llaman sus empleados, acude todas las mañanas a la inmensa nave que Ale-Hop tiene en Oliva (Valencia), a pocos kilómetros de su pueblo natal, Gata de Gorgos (Alicante), donde empezó todo, y se pone a trabajar armado de bolígrafo y libreta. A su alrededor, jóvenes empleados trastean en una recreación a escala de una de sus tiendas de accesorios y artículos de regalo, omnipresentes en playas, estaciones, aeropuertos y calles comerciales de España, Italia, Portugal y Croacia y reconocibles por la escultura de una vaca a tamaño natural a la puerta. Grimalt se dispone, afabilísimo, a la charla acompañado de Raúl, uno de sus cuatro hijos que, lleva, junto a dos de sus hermanos, el día a día de esta empresa familiar. Es el hijo quien cuenta la anécdota: un año, en las vísperas de Fallas, se organizó un concurso de creación de ninots entre los empleados y el que más le gustó a su padre fue uno en el que se le representaba con su perenne bolígrafo enganchado del bolsillo de la camisa y un manchurrón de tinta. Y si le gustó es porque era él, en esencia. Animada por el buen humor del ambiente, saco un objeto del bolso y se lo muestro al dueño de todo esto. Seguir leyendo LA VACA QUE VENDE Desde los 15 años, Vicente Grimalt (Gata de Gorgos, Alicante, 75 años) quería ganarse la vida, y disfrutar de ella, saliendo y sin salir, a la vez, de su pueblo. Hijo de agricultores, supo aprovechar la tradición artesana de su localidad, especializada en la cestería y el mimbre, y el auge del turismo, para vender artículos de regalo a todo el mundo. Tiene 360 tiendas entre España, Italia, Francia, Portugal y Croacia, situadas en lugares de paso, que dan empleo a más de 2.600 personas. La firma acaba de rediseñar la imagen de la vaca que da la bienvenida a los clientes en todas y cada una de sus tiendas, y que inspira sus eslóganes con reclamos como: "Estamos como un cencerro" o "Somos la leche". En 2025, su empresa matriz, Clave Denia, facturó 170 millones de euros.

items.title: ¿Cuánto se inflan los precios en los anuncios de venta de pisos? Del 11% en Madrid al 35% en Granada
items.description: ¿Cuánto se puede rebajar el precio de un piso? La duda ronda a miles de compradores cada vez que ven un anuncio, y la respuesta no es la misma en Madrid que en Bilbao o Sevilla. Pero hay un punto de partida: de media, los pisos se anuncian un 15% por encima de lo que finalmente se paga. Así lo revela un análisis de EL PAÍS en 57 ciudades, que ha cruzado los anuncios de Idealista con los precios reales de las escrituras notariales. Detrás de esa cifra conviven la negociación habitual y una brecha creciente: los vendedores siguen mirando a los años de fuertes subidas, mientras los compradores llegan al límite de su bolsillo. items.title: El mejor verano de nuestras vidas
items.description: Que los incendios no son como eran , lo sabemos. Que las temperaturas no son las mismas, lo sufrimos a diario. Que España brillaba y atraía por su clima, lo recordamos; de que España es el país europeo más vulnerable ante los desafíos del clima, estamos advertidos. Que las olas de calor comienzan antes , lo estamos experimentando. Que una ola se funde con la siguiente, lo padecemos. Que el paisaje es el corazón del patriotismo es algo que se entiende de veras cuando se pierde. Que algo tan aparentemente cerebral como los impuestos está directamente relacionado con ese patrimonio del corazón es una evidencia que solo pueden negar los embusteros negacionistas o los que solo se codean con ellos. Que hasta este año la culpa de todo la tenían esos malvados medioambientalistas que impedían limpiar el monte y los ríos de hierbajos es un bulo propagado por quienes quieren eximir de responsabilidad a quienes manejan los presupuestos. Que construir cortafuegos para apagar esa mentira que, sobre todo en el mundo rural se convierte en un lugar común, es urgente. Que este año esa estúpida frase, “siempre ha hecho calor”, que brota de tantas bocas está muriendo por achicharramiento es algo que va percibiéndose. Que los ancianos saben que el calor de este mes no ha sido el calor que ellos padecieron en su juventud es una verdad que su cuerpo experimenta . Que España es un país diverso constituido en comunidades autónomas es algo ya natural en nuestras vidas, como comienza a serlo que no somos nadie si no sabemos colaborar, que las rencillas o las separaciones no responden a la realidad cuando esta se impone con furia. Nada que ver con el día anterior, cuando el alcalde, Javier Úbeda, reconoce que pasaron un mal rato hasta que el viento cambió de dirección. El fuego del gran incendio que arrasa el suroeste de la Comunidad de Madrid ha afectado a pequeños pueblos de la zona rural, la más periférica de la región. De haber penetrado hacia la capital, las llamas hubieran afectado a los municipios acomodados y mucho más poblados como Villanueva de la Cañada, Villaviciosa de Odón o Boadilla, donde se asientan lo que algunos llaman urbanizaciones bosque, entornos privilegiados pero expuestos al peligro de los incendios. Son expresiones culturales que han trascendido su tiempo y no se quedan atrás, generación tras generación, con las que es imposible la nostalgia y siempre posible el negocio. Así es Spiderman, cuya industria ofrece continuamente productos para personas de toda edad y condición. Sigue hecho, literalmente, un chaval. El juez José Luis Calama había citado para el martes como investigado a Julio Martínez Martínez, amigo del expresidente del Gobierno y administrador de Análisis Relevante, la empresa en el epicentro de la trama . La cita se presumía determinante ante la duda de si el empresario respaldaría la versión de Zapatero, que declaró en junio y aseguró que era ajeno a la creación y administración de esa sociedad y solo trabajó y cobró de ella como consultor externo, o si, por el contrario, desmentiría ese relato y corroboraría el de los investigadores, que sitúan al expresidente a los mandos del entramado. Martínez Martínez no esperó a estar ante el juez y, en la víspera de su citación, entregó en la Audiencia Nacional un documento en el que se ofrecía a colaborar con la justicia y señalaba a Zapatero. Comenzó así un movimiento en cadena a l que se sumaron Julio Martínez Sola y Roberto Roselli , también imputados y hasta entonces máximos directivos de la aerolínea Plus Ultra (dimitieron este viernes tras ser citados por el juez), que endosa al exlíder socialista la máxima responsabilidad en los hechos que se investigan. items.title: PTI slams govt over Rs1.8bn package for bureaucrats
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Saturday criticised the government for continuously increasing fuel prices while simultaneously allowing a Rs1.8 billion special allowance package for top bureaucrats who already receive free fuel. PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said ordinary Pakis­tanis were subjected to a six-day petroleum monsoon that drove petrol to Rs335.18 and diesel to Rs383.46 per litre. He observed that the rulers have perfected a dual system: free fuel and luxuries for the elite, and daily fuel bombs for the public. Agriculture, transport and industry are being systematically executed under the excuse of international markets. “PTI demands the immediate rollback of the six-day cumulative hike; a sharp cut in the Rs80 per litre petroleum levy and the overall Rs1.7 trillion levy target; and the complete scrap of the disastrous daily pricing mechanism,” Mr Akram said. He added that Rs1.8 billion bure­aucratic bonus should be cancelled. On the agricultural front, Mr Akram called the government’s sudden decision to import 1.1 million metric tonnes of wheat the most transparent fraud. After claiming a bumper harvest of over 29m tonnes against a domestic consumption of 27m tonnes, he said the sudden shortage and the mysterious disappearance of 4.5m tonnes raised questions of monumental incompetence. “PTI demands full transparency on production and stock figures, an immediate forensic audit of the missing 4.5m tonnes, the declaration of an agricultural emergency, cancellation of unnecessary imports, and an immediate announcement of next season’s minimum support price,” he said. In Sindh, Mr Akram accused the provincial government of reducing the Sindh Public Service Commission’s 2024 exam results to a political marketplace, demanding an independent forensic audit and the cancellation of tainted results. In Azad Kashmir, he condemned what he described as the ruling alliance’s pre-poll theatrics. Dispatching 10 electric buses adorned with Maryam Nawaz’s photographs, funded by Punjab taxpayers, constitutes open electoral bribery and a mockery of the election code, Mr Akram said. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Auto-écoles : vers une réforme de la formation et des conditions d’agrément
items.description: Le secteur des auto-écoles s’apprête à connaître une importante réforme destinée à moderniser l’enseignement de la conduite au Maroc. Les changements envisagés concernent notamment les conditions d’ouverture des établissements, les exigences de formation des candidats, la gestion des véhicules d’apprentissage ainsi que la numérisation des procédures administratives. Selon les conclusions d’une réunion de coordination tenue entre l’Agence nationale de la sécurité routière (NARSA) et les représentants des auto-écoles, plusieurs propositions de modification du cahier des charges ont fait l’objet d’un consensus. Certaines dispositions ne pourront toutefois entrer en vigueur qu’après l’adoption des textes réglementaires nécessaires à leur application. Parmi les principales nouveautés figure un durcissement des conditions d’accès à la profession. La caution provisoire exigée lors de la demande d’autorisation passerait de 20.000 à 100.000 dirhams. La caution définitive, fixée au même montant, devrait quant à elle être maintenue pendant une période de deux ans après la délivrance de l’agrément. La réforme prévoit également que chaque auto-école dispose d’au moins deux véhicules légers dont elle est propriétaire. Le recours à des véhicules loués ne serait plus autorisé. Les établissements devront en outre justifier d’une capacité financière suffisante, se doter d’un système informatique connecté aux services de la NARSA et utiliser des supports pédagogiques homologués. Le texte ouvre également la possibilité d’intégrer des simulateurs de conduite dans les dispositifs de formation. Sur le plan pédagogique, une révision du volume horaire minimal de formation est également à l’étude. Le nombre d’heures consacrées à l’enseignement théorique, actuellement fixé à 20 heures, pourrait être porté à 30 heures afin de mieux préparer les candidats aux nouvelles exigences de l’examen du permis de conduire. Le délai de dépôt des dossiers pour l’épreuve théorique devrait, lui aussi, être allongé, passant de 20 à 30 jours. Le projet prévoit par ailleurs d’encadrer juridiquement les situations de fermeture ou de cessation d’activité des auto-écoles, afin de garantir la continuité de la formation des candidats. Enfin, la NARSA envisage de généraliser le système de voiture connectée « Smart Drive Test », reposant sur l’intelligence artificielle, dans le but de rendre l’évaluation de l’épreuve pratique plus transparente, plus objective et davantage automatisée. The post Auto-écoles : vers une réforme de la formation et des conditions d’agrément appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: On first visit to Syria in 17 years, UN chief meets Sharaa
items.description: Syria’s President Ahmed al-Sharaa receives UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres at presidential palace.—AFP • Guterres pledges support for Syria’s reconstruction; backs Syria’s request for EU support; calls situation in Golan Heights ‘totally unacceptable’ • Damascus demands Israeli withdrawal from ‘buffer zone’ DAMASCUS: UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres pledged help for Syrian reconstruction on Saturday during the first visit to Damascus by a serving United Nations chief since 2009, before the start of a civil war that killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions. Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa received Guterres at the presidential palace in Damascus, state news agency SANA said, without providing further details. “No country emerges from a very severe conflict and rebuilds itself on its own,” Guterres said after the talks with Sharaa at a joint press conference with Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani. “We must help Syria in its determination and resolve to do so,” Guterres added. Shaibani reiterated Syria’s request for more support from the international community, especially the European Union. He said Guterres’ talks with Sharaa which Shaibani also attended had focused on increasing UN support for reconstruction and a government plan to close displacement camps. Guterres also said the situation around Syria’s Golan Heights was unacceptable, as the Syrian foreign minister urged Israeli forces to withdraw from a UN-patrolled buffer zone where they deployed in 2024. “What is happening in the region around the Golan Heights is totally unacceptable,” Guterres added. Shaibani called for an “immediate and unconditional Israeli withdrawal” from the area where they had advanced. Guterres’ visit is another milestone for Syria since rebels ousted President Bashar al-Assad in late 2024, ending the war that began in 2011 and launching a transitional period. At the time, Guterres described “the end of the Syrian dictatorship” under Assad as a sign of hope for the region. In a post on X on Saturday for what he described as a “visit of solidarity”, Guterres said: “The United Nations stands with Syria at this pivotal moment.” Guterres will also meet other government officials and representatives of Syrian civil society and is expected to address the country’s parliament on Monday, UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said earlier this week. He will underline that the country has an opportunity “not only to recover from conflict, but also to lay the foundations for a future for Syria that will be more stable, more inclusive, and more prosperous for all Syrians”, Dujarric said. Return to global stage Guterres is expected to be in Damascus for several days, but the full schedule of his visit has not been released by his office. He is visiting just weeks after two bombs exploded near a hotel in Damascus where French President Emmanuel Macron spent the night, overshadowing the first visit to Syria by a European Union head of state since Assad was toppled. Sharaa’s government is seeking to rebuild Syria’s international ties and economy after nearly 14 years of war and decades of isolation under the Assad family’s rule. Sharaa, who broke ties with al Qaeda in 2016, led an alliance of rebel factions that ousted Assad in a lightning offensive in December 2024. Since taking power, his government has sought to re-establish Syria’s diplomatic ties to expand beyond Assad’s longtime allies, Russia and Iran. Last year, Sharaa became the first Syrian president since 1967 to take part in the UN General Assembly in New York. The US has lifted most sanctions on Syria and President Donald Trump informed Sharaa earlier this month that he intended to remove Syria from Washington’s list of state sponsors of terrorism. Guterres is also expected during his trip to visit a UN peacekeeping force that has maintained a buffer zone between Israeli and Syrian forces for decades, Dujarric said. Israeli troops have occupied new areas in southern Syria after Assad was ousted. Dama­scus has demanded they withdraw and return to a 1974 disengagement agreement. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Ravi, Chenab flood levels likely to reach medium to high today
items.description: LAHORE: While a vast area of Punjab, covering nearly 400 square kilometres, has come under water following ongoing torrential rains and the overflow of several drains carrying water far beyond their designed capacity, the Chenab and Ravi rivers are expected to reach medium to high flood levels over the next 24 hours. The warning at a time when the flooding has already caused widespread damage to standing crops, livestock and infrastructure prompted district administrations in several areas to expedite flood-response measures, including the establishment of relief camps. “The situation is very alarming this time, as a vast area of around 400sq-kms has come under water in Sheikhupura, Muridke, Gujranwala, Narowal, Sambrial and Pasrur, which fall within the Lahore and Gujranwala divisions,” a senior official of the Punjab irrigation department told Dawn on Saturday. “The current situation resembles an inland sea because of the vast expanse of floodwater,” the official added, requesting anonymity. Floodwaters swamp large swathes of Punjab The situation is both unprecedented and highly challenging during the ongoing monsoon season, according to the official. “Let me tell you that the flow in the Ravi at Shahdara (Lahore) is 22,000 cusecs, whereas at Balloki (downstream) it has surged to 87,000 cusecs. The question is: where did the additional 65,000 cusecs come from? It is water flowing into the river through drains and rainfall,” he explained. “Ordinarily, the flow in the Ravi should decrease by the time it reaches Balloki. Instead, it has increased,” the official said, adding that it could take another three to four days for the situation to return to normal, provided there is no further rainfall. According to the Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological Department, the Chenab and Ravi rivers are currently flowing at medium and low flood levels, respectively. However, water levels in both rivers are expected to rise to medium to high flood levels over the next 24 hours. The Chenab at Marala, Khanki and Qadirabad is expected to remain at medium to high flood levels, while the Ravi is also likely to reach similar levels at Balloki (Kasur) and Sidhnai (Khanewal). “River Chenab at Khanki, Qadirabad and Chiniot Bridge is at the medium flood level. River Indus at Kalabagh, Chashma and Taunsa, River Kabul at Nowshera, River Chenab at Marala and Trimmu, and River Ravi at Balloki and Sidhnai are at the low flood level. All major rivers at other gauging stations are flowing within their normal ranges,” the FFD report states. As more showers are expected on Sunday, the deputy commissioners of Lahore, Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Narowal, Khanewal and others have been put on high-alert in terms of flood monitoring and preparedness arrangements. The Lahore DC and his team rushed to the affected areas in the catchment area of Hudiara drain. They visited Tiba Khudpur Road and the Hadyara Drain in Mohlanwal to review drainage operations and monitor the flow of rainwater following heavy monsoon showers across the city. The Lahore commissioner also visited Nankana Sahib to review the flood situation and emergency response arrangements. He visited Halla Waraich and inspected the river erosion occurring beyond the village. During the visit, he was briefed about evacuation, rescue, and relief arrangements and measures. He directed the district administration to desilt the choking points of Nullah Dek. Khanewal DC Hena Arshad visited Sidhnai headworks, the Mai Safura Bund Breaching Section, Kund Sargana and Fazil Shah Bund to inspect flood protection arrangements and review preparedness measures. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Cabinet panel approves prices of 52 life-saving medicines
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A sub-committee of the federal cabinet, headed by Fin­ance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, has approved the prices of 52 life-saving drugs, prompting Health Minister Mustafa Kamal to say that patients would finally have access to cheaper and better-quality medicines. “However, the approval is subject to the final approval of the federal cabinet,” Mr Kamal said while speaking to Dawn on Saturday. The sub-committee, headed by Mr Aurangzeb, has five members, including the health minister. Replying to a question, Mr Kamal said that there were two categories under which medicine prices could be increased. “The first category is hardship [under which prices are increased when production becomes unviable due to rising production costs], and the second category is only the fixation of prices for new molecules. “All 52 medicines were placed under the price-fixation category,” he said. The federal health minister said that the majority of the molecules were either new to the market or alternatives to some of the existing molecules. When asked about the nature of the medicines, he told Dawn that they were intended to treat a range of diseases, including cancer and diabetes, and also included vaccines. “If the federal cabinet approves these medicines, the public will have access to cheaper, high-quality medicines in the market,” he said, while expressing the hope that the cabinet would give approval. “Once they are approved, production will begin, and they will be made available to consumers,” the federal health minister said. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Seven killed, 20 hurt as heavy rains lash Punjab
items.description: LAHORE: At least seven people, including two children, were killed and 20 others injured in rain-related incidents across Punjab during the last 24 hours, while downpour also damaged houses and killed livestock, according to the Provincial Disaster Management Authority. The PDMA report, available with Dawn , said 14 rain-related incidents were reported across the province up to 2pm on Saturday. These included deaths caused by structural collapses and drowning, injuries from roof collapses and electrocution, the collapse of seven house roofs, and the death of five buffaloes. In Lahore, three people, including a man, a woman and a child, died, while five others were injured in four separate roof-collapse incidents in Bobby Plaza, Garhi Shahu Railway Colony, Saggian Pind and Kahna. Two people, including a man and a child, were killed and three others, including a woman and two children, were injured when the roof of a house collapsed near Adda Dhing Shah on Depalpur Road in Kasur. A woman died after the roof of a house collapsed due to heavy rain in Faisalabad, while a child drowned in rainwater that had accumulated in fields near Pathan Colony in Gujranwala. Three people, including a man and two children, were injured when the roof of a house collapsed, while another man suffered injuries after being electrocuted by an electric pole during the rain in Bahawalnagar. In Narowal, two women were injured in a roof-collapse incident in Sair Bajwa village, while a woman was injured after the roof of her house collapsed in Sialkot’s Darma Wala neighbourhood. In Nankana Sahib and Sheikhupura, three women sustained injuries in two separate roof-collapse incidents at Dera Mehboob Alam and near Peer Shah Khaki Diwan Darbar. In Okara, two men were injured after an animal shed collapsed due to rain. Addressing a press conference at the PDMA headquarters, Director General Umar Abbas said Punjab remained largely safe from flooding despite the ongoing monsoon spell, with water levels in all major rivers, including the Ravi and Sutlej, remaining within normal limits. He said the heaviest rainfall during the current spell had been recor­ded in the Gujranwala and Rawalp­indi divisions, particularly in Naro­wal, Jhelum and Gujrat districts. He said a breach in the Dek Nullah near Narowal and another in an embankment in Sheikhupura had been plugged immediately, averting any major damage. He said monsoon-related incidents had so far claimed 22 lives and left 183 people injured across Punjab. He said any emergency could be reported through the Rescue 1122 helpline, adding that the authorities were also monitoring ageing electricity infrastructure to minimise power-related accidents during the rainy season. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Mirpur heads to polls amid barbs, warnings
items.description: • Maryam shares video of green buses reaching AJK • PPP alleges code of conduct violations by rivals • Election commissioner warns against new schemes, reviews election preparations • 2,316 polling stations set up across division • MQM-P withdraws candidates in PML-N’s favour MUZAFFARABAD: The Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and its coalition partner at the Centre, the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), are set to face off in the Mirpur Division elections on Monday, as electioneering ended at midnight amid allegations of pre-poll rigging by the PPP and a warning from the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission that no individual or institution would be allowed to violate the election code of conduct. The Election Commission on Saturday reiterated that no individual or institution would be allowed to violate the election code of conduct, amid a controversy over development promises made during the election campaign. Although the commission’s statement did not name any individual or political party, it came after ex-PM Nawaz Sharif and Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz, while addressing election rallies in Muzaffarabad and Mirpur, promised electric buses and mobile hospitals. The announcements prompted the PPP to approach the Election Commission, urging it to take notice of what it described as blatant violations of the election code of conduct and election laws. In a related political development, MQM-P annou­nced its support for PML-N candidates in the AJK elections by withdrawing its own candidates. The announcement came after the PML-N delegation, led by its Sindh President Bashir Memon and Mini­ster of State for Religious Affairs and Interfaith Har­m­­ony Kheal Das Kohistani, met MQM-P leaders at the party’s Bahadurabad headquarters in Karachi. Speaking to reporters afterwards, MQM-P leader Dr Farooq Sattar said his party’s candidates contesting from various constituencies, including seats reserved for refugees, would withdraw in favour of PML-N nominees. He said a PML-N victory in the Azad Kashmir elections would also be a victory for the MQM-P. An Election Commission spokesperson said federal and provincial ministers were free to participate in electioneering in AJK but could not use official protocol, government resources or the state machinery for electoral purposes. “The announcement of any new development scheme, financial package, public facility or welfare project during the election campaign will amount to a violation of the code of conduct. Any vehicles, equipment, relief goods or other facilities sent by the federal or provincial governments during the election period will be confiscated and action taken in accordance with the law,” he said. The spokesperson urged all ministers, candidates and political parties to str­ictly observe the code of con­­­­­­duct to ensure free, fair and transparent elections and maintain public confidence in the electoral process. Earlier on Saturday afte­rnoon, Chief Minister Mar­y­­am Nawaz confirmed that the green buses had reac­hed Muzaffarabad, sha­­r­ing a video showing several of the vehicles carrying posters featuring her portrait alongside local PML-N leaders. The controversy had escalated a day earlier when PPP Secretary Gen­eral Nayyar Hussain Bukh­a­­­ri met Chief Election Com­­­­­m­issioner Ghulam Mu­­­­­s­­­­tafa Mughal and sought action over the transfer of 10 electric buses bearing Ms Nawaz’s picture to the AJK administration. “The Punjab government’s move of handing over electric buses featuring Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s photos to the AJK government is political bribery,” Mr Bukhari had said. In a post on the party’s X account on Saturday, Mr Bukhari said he had also sought a no-objection certificate from the commission to launch a “motivation service” in AJK as part of the party’s manifesto and election campaign. He did not elaborate on the nature of the proposed service. Mr Bukhari at a press conference in Muzaffara­bad reiterated his party’s concerns over the alleged violations of the election code of conduct. He demanded an immediate ban on the participation of federal ministers and the Punjab chief minister in the election campaign and urged the Election Comm­ission to ensure strict enforcement of the code. He maintained that while the PPP was not opposed to providing public facilities, it could not help but ask why such initiatives were being announced only during the election campaign. “If the Punjab government genuinely wished to extend such facilities to AJK, it could have done so before the announcement of the election schedule or after the polls,” he said. He said the Election Commission should take imm­­­ediate notice of the matter; otherwise, the code of conduct would lose its credibility. Around the same time, PPP Central Information Secretary Shazia Marri posted a statement on X, saying Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari was striving for “a bright and empowered future” for the people of Kashmir. She said the PPP chairman had raised the slogans of the right to rule, right to property and right to empl­o­­­yment for Kashmiris, adding: “This is not a crime.” Ms Marri asked the PML-N to present its programme for Kashmir instead of attacking its political opponents. CEC chairs meeting Meanwhile, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal chaired a meeting in Mirpur to review preparations for the 2026 general elections. The meeting was atte­nded by Election Commi­ssion Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel, Dist­r­­ict Returning Officers Jah­­­­­angir Ahmed Jaral (Mirpur), Muhammad Idr­ees Bhatti (Kotli) and Hafiz Sardar Muhammad Akram Khan (Bhimber), returning officers, Mirpur Divisional Commissioner Raja Tahir Mumtaz, Dep­uty Inspector General of Police Kamran Ali, and others. After the DROs briefed the meeting on election arrangements in their res­p­­ective districts, Comm­­issioner Mumtaz said all preparations for the elections had been finalised across the three districts of Mirpur Division. He said the division had 1,400,437 registered voters, comprising 724,811 men and 675,626 women. A total of 2,316 polling stations had been established, including 1,241 dec­lared highly sensitive, 724 sensitive and 351 normal. He said LA-3 (Mirpur City) had the highest number of contestants, with 34 candidates, while 288 candidates were contesting elections across the division’s 13 constituencies. To oversee polling and security arrangements, the administration had established 13 zones and 205 sectors across the division, wi­­­­th enhanced security mea­­­­­sures at sensitive and highly sensitive polling stations. DIG Ali told the meeting that 18,560 personnel from the police and other law enforcement agencies wou­ld be deployed across Mir­pur Division for security. The deployment inclu­des 5,536 personnel in Mirpur district, 4,504 in Bh­imber and 8,520 in Kot­li. He said a three-tier security plan had been devised under which the police would serve as the first tier, civil armed forces as the second, and the Pakistan Army as the third. The second tier would comprise personnel from the Pakistan Rangers (Punjab), Pakistan Ran­gers (Sindh) and the Federal Constabulary, while 2,100 Pakistan Army troops would also be deployed to assist with election security. The DIG said all security forces would perform their duties under an integrated security plan on polling day, July 27. Meanwhile, AJK Secretary Information Muhammad Rashid Hanif and Director Information Tariq Jamil Durrani urged journalists and media organisations to ensure responsible, impartial and professional coverage of the elections. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

items.title: Concours de médecine : une enquête ouverte après des soupçons de fuite des sujets
items.description: Le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur a saisi les autorités judiciaires après la diffusion, sur les réseaux sociaux, de contenus présentés comme les sujets du concours commun d’accès aux facultés de médecine, de pharmacie et de médecine dentaire. L’enquête devra déterminer l’authenticité de ces documents et établir d’éventuelles responsabilités. Le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche scientifique et de l’Innovation a annoncé l’ouverture d’une enquête judiciaire à la suite de la circulation, sur les réseaux sociaux et certaines applications de messagerie, de contenus présentés comme les sujets du concours commun d’accès aux facultés de médecine, de pharmacie et de médecine dentaire au titre de l’année universitaire 2026-2027. Dans un communiqué, le département indique avoir saisi les autorités judiciaires compétentes afin de vérifier l’authenticité des documents diffusés et d’établir, le cas échéant, les responsabilités conformément aux dispositions légales en vigueur. Le ministère précise qu’il prendra toutes les mesures qui s’imposeront à la lumière des conclusions de l’enquête, afin de préserver l’intégrité et la transparence des concours d’accès aux établissements d’enseignement supérieur, tout en garantissant le principe d’égalité des chances entre les candidats. À ce stade, aucune fuite n’a été officiellement confirmée. Les autorités n’ont validé ni l’authenticité des documents relayés en ligne ni l’existence d’une compromission des épreuves. Les investigations en cours devront permettre d’établir les faits et de déterminer les suites à donner. Le concours concerné s’est tenu le 18 juillet 2026, après une présélection fondée sur les résultats du baccalauréat. Cette année, 7.340 places étaient proposées dans les établissements publics, réparties entre 5.790 places en médecine, 1.090 en pharmacie et 460 en médecine dentaire. Les listes principales des admis ont été publiées le 21 juillet, tandis que les inscriptions administratives doivent débuter le 28 juillet, conformément au calendrier fixé par le ministère. Dans son communiqué, le ministère rappelle enfin que les facultés de médecine, de pharmacie et de médecine dentaire du Royaume répondent à des standards académiques et scientifiques reconnus aux niveaux national et international. The post Concours de médecine : une enquête ouverte après des soupçons de fuite des sujets appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Sénégal : le président Diomaye Faye a créé son propre parti pour réorganiser son camp politique et consolider sa majorité
items.description: Le président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye a annoncé samedi la création d’un nouveau parti politique baptisé « Kiray – Les Nationalistes Républicains », dans le but de réorganiser son camp politique et de consolider sa majorité, à la suite de sa rupture avec son ancien allié Ousmane Sonko et du remaniement du paysage politique du pays. Cette annonce a été faite lors du congrès fondateur du parti qui s’est tenu à Dakar. Les dirigeants de la coalition « Diomaye Président » ont décidé de transformer cette coalition en un parti politique constituant une base de soutien au président en vue des prochaines échéances électorales, tout en cherchant à fédérer les partis, mouvements et personnalités favorables à son programme. Dans son discours, le président sénégalais avait déclaré que la création du parti représentait un « engagement » envers les Sénégalais, ajoutant que ce que les années passées avaient gâché « il nous incombe de le réparer », appelant à restaurer l’esprit de consensus national et à préserver l’héritage du pays au profit des générations futures. Le président sénégalais a souligné que le nouveau parti se fondera sur des principes avant toute quête de pouvoir, précisant que l’éthique sera le fondement de son action et que l’adhésion à ce parti se fera au service de l’intérêt général et non dans un but de gain personnel. Il a ajouté que les responsabilités au sein du parti seraient « des devoirs et non des récompenses », et que personne « ne trouverait refuge face à ses erreurs », soulignant que la justice au Sénégal « est indépendante et le restera ». Faye s’est également engagé à ce que le parti adopte le principe de transparence financière, précisant que ses ressources seraient rendues publiques et gérées de manière transparente, et que l’argent resterait un moyen au service de l’action politique et non une fin en soi. Le lancement de ce nouveau parti intervient à un moment où la scène politique sénégalaise connaît un remaniement des alignements après la rupture entre Faye et Sonko. En créant sa propre structure partisane, le président cherche à consolider sa majorité politique et à se préparer aux prochains scrutins, au premier rang desquels les élections locales prévues l’année prochaine.

items.title: Une délégation du congrès américain salue le rôle joué par la Mauritanie dans la lutte contre le terrorisme
items.description: Une délégation du Congrès américain a salué le niveau de sécurité et de stabilité en Mauritanie ainsi que le rôle joué par ce pays dans la lutte contre le terrorisme et le crime organisé dans la région du Sahel, lors d'entretiens avec le ministre mauritanien des Affaires étrangères, Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, à Nouakchott, selon un communiqué du ministère mauritanien des Affaires étrangères. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères a indiqué que la rencontre avait porté sur les moyens de renforcer les relations bilatérales entre la Mauritanie et les États-Unis, notamment dans les domaines de la sécurité, de l’économie et de l’investissement, dans le cadre d’une visite de travail effectuée par la délégation américaine en Mauritanie. La délégation comprenait des membres de la Chambre des représentants américaine, parmi lesquels Austin Scott, Salud Carvajal, membre de la commission des forces armées, et Jimmy Panetta, membre de la commission des moyens et des ressources. Le ministère a ajouté que le ministre mauritanien avait souligné lors de cette rencontre que son pays avait préservé sa sécurité et sa stabilité malgré les défis sécuritaires dans la région du Sahel, en adoptant une approche alliant sécurité et développement. Les deux parties ont également examiné le renforcement de la coopération dans les domaines de la formation, du renforcement des capacités, de la sécurité maritime, de la sécurité des frontières et de la cybersécurité, ainsi que les opportunités d’investissement dans les secteurs du gaz naturel, des minéraux et des énergies renouvelables. Le ministère a indiqué que les membres de la délégation américaine avaient exprimé leur intérêt pour le renforcement de la coopération économique et des investissements avec la Mauritanie, ainsi que la poursuite de la coordination sur les questions de sécurité et de stabilité régionale.

items.title: Droits humains : le CNDH et le HCP s’allient pour évaluer l'effectivité des libertés
items.description: Passer des intentions juridiques à la mesure concrète du réel. Le Conseil national des droits de l'homme (CNDH) et le Haut-Commissariat au Plan (HCP) ont officialisé, mercredi à Rabat, un partenariat stratégique visant à établir un système national d’indicateurs des droits et des libertés. Signée par la présidente du CNDH, Amina Bouayach, et le Haut-Commissaire au Plan, Chakib Benmoussa, cette convention s’inscrit dans la continuité de la stratégie d’« effectivité des droits » impulsée par le Conseil dès 2019. L’objectif affiché est d'adosser le suivi et l'évaluation de la situation sociétale du pays à des données probantes et vérifiables. Une alliance entre institution normative et référence statistique L'accord scelle un rapprochement institutionnel entre l’organe chargé de la protection et de la promotion des droits humains au Maroc et l'institution nationale de référence en matière de statistique, d'analyse et de prospective. Ensemble, les deux structures entendent concevoir une plate-forme d'indicateurs bâtie sur des méthodes scientifiques alignées sur les standards internationaux. Ce dispositif doit permettre de suivre l’évolution des droits fondamentaux dans le Royaume, d'évaluer l’impact réel des politiques publiques et de mesurer les progrès accomplis. « Ce projet s’inscrit dans le cadre des mutations actuelles du système de protection des droits humains », a souligné Amina Bouayach, évoquant une « étape qualitative » pour le Conseil. « Il exige de passer du discours normatif à une approche par indicateurs, capable de mesurer l'écart entre ce qui est garanti par la loi et la réalité vécue par les citoyennes et les citoyens ». Pour la présidente du CNDH, cette démarche vise à élever le débat public annuel sur les droits de l'homme : dépasser le simple cadre législatif et théorique pour concentrer l'attention sur l'impact concret des règles en vigueur au quotidien. S'appuyer sur la donnée pour réduire les fractures territoriales De son côté, le Haut-Commissaire au Plan, Chakib Benmoussa, a rappelé la portée de cette signature, qui intervient dans un contexte de réforme institutionnelle marqué par l’adoption récente de deux textes fondamentaux : l'un restructurant le HCP et élargissant ses prérogatives, l'autre réorganisant le système statistique national pour en renforcer la gouvernance. Selon Benmoussa, cette transformation s’appuie sur l'ouverture et le partage d'expertises au sein de l'écosystème de la donnée — un préalable indispensable à une action publique éclairée et ajustée aux besoins de la population. « L’évaluation de l’effectivité des droits ne peut être complète sans données fiables et outils d’analyse précis », a-t-il affirmé, précisant que ce futur mécanisme permettra de repérer les poches de vulnérabilité et les disparités, notamment à l'échelle territoriale, afin d'orienter les politiques de développement vers plus de justice spatiale et d'inclusion. Formation, tableaux de bord et standards internationaux Concrètement, le document fixe plusieurs axes de travail conjoints. L'Alimentation statistique qui consiste à la mise à disposition de données indispensables pour nourrir le système national et alimenter les rapports d'analyse sectoriels. Des outils de pilotage qui consiste au déploiement d’un tableau de bord national destiné à suivre les données aux niveaux national et régional, afin de repérer les déséquilibres locaux et d’éclairer les décisions publiques. Aussi, la standardisation qui consiste au développement de méthodologies de mesure conformes aux directives du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies aux droits de l'homme (HCDH) et enfin le renforcement des compétences avec le déploiement d'ateliers techniques et de sessions de formation au profit des cadres des deux institutions. Cette dynamique prolonge les travaux amorcés lors du premier atelier technique national sur les indicateurs des droits humains, réuni le 29 janvier 2026 en présence d'experts et de partenaires internationaux. Une rencontre qui avait posé les jalons d'un cadre d'évaluation scientifique et objectif, tourné vers la mesure de l'impact réel des politiques publiques au Maroc. The post Droits humains : le CNDH et le HCP s’allient pour évaluer l'effectivité des libertés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.description: Le ministre mauritanien de la Défense, Hanena Ould Sidi, a examiné samedi, avec une délégation de la Chambre des représentants américaine, les moyens de renforcer la coopération entre Nouakchott et Washington dans le domaine de la défense, lors d'une rencontre qui a réuni les deux parties dans la capitale mauritanienne. L'armée mauritanienne a indiqué que la délégation américaine était présidée par Austin Scott, membre de la commission des forces armées de la Chambre des représentants, et comprenait la chargée d'affaires par intérim de l'ambassade des États-Unis à Nouakchott, Corina R. Sanders, ainsi que l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade, le lieutenant-colonel Malik Shkhram. Plusieurs responsables militaires mauritaniens ont assisté à la réunion, parmi lesquels le secrétaire général du ministère de la Défense, le colonel Ishaq Abdoullah Mahmoud Brahim, le directeur du Bureau de la documentation et de la sécurité militaire, le colonel Hassan Abdi Vleïvil, le directeur des relations extérieures, le colonel Cheikh Mohamed Lemine Bilal, et le directeur du Bureau de coordination, le colonel Manga Soba.

items.title: Guinée : le ministère de la Fonction publique dément tout recrutement de 20 000 agents et met en garde contre les fausses annonces
items.description: Le Ministère de la Modernisation de l'Administration et de la Fonction publique a opposé un démenti catégorique aux informations relayées ces derniers jours sur les réseaux sociaux, faisant état d'un prétendu lancement d'un concours de recrutement de 20 000 agents dans la fonction publique. Dans un communiqué rendu public, le département qualifie ces informations de « totalement infondées » et appelle les citoyens, en particulier les jeunes diplômés et les demandeurs d’emploi, à ne pas se laisser tromper par ces rumeurs. Il (ministère) précise qu'aucun avis de concours n'a été publié à ce jour, que ce soit pour le recrutement de 20 000 agents ou pour tout autre effectif. Il insiste sur le fait que toute procédure de recrutement dans la fonction publique fera l'objet d'une communication officielle à travers ses canaux habilités, notamment son site internet, sa page Meta et la presse nationale. Il rappelle également que l'accès aux emplois publics est régi par la loi L/2019/027/AN du 9 juin 2019 portant statut général des agents de l'État, qui prévoit le recrutement par voie de concours. Face à la prolifération des fausses informations sur les plateformes numériques, le ministère invite les citoyens à faire preuve de la plus grande vigilance afin d'éviter les tentatives d'escroquerie et d'arnaque liées à de faux recrutements. Enfin, le Ministère de la Modernisation de l'Administration et de la Fonction publique souligne que toute information officielle relative à un éventuel concours de recrutement sera systématiquement diffusée sur ses plateformes de communication accréditées. items.title: Mohamed Brahmi, un symbole de courage et de dignité, toujours vivant dans les mémoires
items.description: À l'occasion du triste anniversaire de l'assassinat de Mohamed Brahmi, sa famille, soutenue par des militants, des syndicalistes et de nombreux citoyens, s'est rassemblée pour honorer la mémoire de cet homme tombé en martyr le 25 juillet 2013. En ce jour de mémoire, l'émotion était vive au cimetière du Jellaz, où personnalités publiques, acteurs de la société civile et proches du défunt se sont recueillis dans une atmosphère empreinte de respect pour réciter la Fatiha à la mémoire de l'ancien député et dirigeant politique. Homme courageux et intègre, Mohamed Brahmi s'est battu pour la démocratie, la défense des libertés et les droits humains, rêvant d'une Tunisie libre et souveraine. Fervent opposant à l'islam politique et au parti Ennahdha, alors au pouvoir, il était reconnu pour ses positions intransigeantes et sa quête permanente de justice sociale et de valeurs républicaines. En ce sombre 25 juillet 2013, Mohamed Brahmi était lâchement assassiné à quelques pas de son domicile. Ce second assassinat politique (survenu quelques mois après celui de son camarade Chokri Belaïd, assassiné le 6 février de la même année ) a déclenché une vague de manifestations à travers tout le pays, de sa ville natale de Sidi Bouzid jusqu'à la capitale. La colère populaire soulevée par ce crime odieux avait alors accéléré la chute du gouvernement d'Ali Larayedh, ouvrant la voie à l'instauration d'un gouvernement de technocrates dirigé par Mehdi Jomaa. Devoir de mémoire : Au-delà du simple recueillement, cette journée réaffirme l'exigence inébranlable de vérité et de justice pour Mohamed Brahmi, symbole immortel de dignité, ainsi que pour l'ensemble des martyrs de la nation. Y. N. L’article Mohamed Brahmi, un symbole de courage et de dignité, toujours vivant dans les mémoires est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: A Brief Exchange That Shows the Enormous Difference Between Trump and Obama
items.description: Suavity is a sorely missed ingredient in the American presidency. The effortless charm of a Roosevelt or a Reagan, a Bush or a Clinton, projected a particular brand of power. Suave means a kind of athletic ease and self-command in difficult, spotlighted circumstances, the assurance that solutions are at hand if only we all hold our composure and act right-headedly. Here was the ultra-suave Barack Obama’s message to the basketball player Caitlin Clark in a small but noteworthy exchange over the WNBA All-Star weekend: It never hurts to be winsome. In fact, it can help you win. Can you imagine Donald Trump in the same situation, what he’d have done or said, the race-baiting and appeal to baseness? As if Trump would even deign to meet a WNBA player, that is. He prefers to use the league’s players from afar for his own purposes. His White House has made the WNBA a flash point for attacks on transgender athletes, and he and his hard-right allies have tried to make Clark out to be a victim of racial violence on the court. Congressional conservatives even called for the federal government to investigate the WNBA for civil-rights violations because of players fouling her. Here is how Trump used another young woman he views as an adversary, the CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins, at the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner yesterday, while Obama was visiting WNBA players in Chicago: After Collins received an award for “excellence under deadline pressure,” Trump barked from the podium that it was a “fake” prize, that she didn’t deserve it, and then he went to some lengths to demean her. Not suave. Not winning. The WNBA has been difficult to watch at times this season, so rife with racial tensions, toxic fan behavior , and carping over officiating that it seems a microcosm of a country in crisis over dirty play in seemingly every societal arena. Much ill will has swirled around Clark, the superstar 24-year-old guard for the Indiana Fever, who can be either mesmerizing to watch or tiresome, depending on how aggrieved she feels on the day. Clark has complained that she is intentionally targeted with hard fouls—and sometimes she is, but not because she’s white. Mauling is the guaranteed, time-honored way to stop an otherwise insuperable player. Clark is the fastest in league history to hit 200 three-pointers , the first to ever score 45 points with 11 assists in a game, and such a head-clutchingly great passer that she can make defenses look like they’re lost. And Clark’s got a plenty hard edge of her own. She can jaw so vociferously at referees that she’s gotten seven technical fouls this season, one away from a suspension. That has done nothing to help calm matters in a league whose product is being torn apart by internal resentments and external malignity. In mid-June, when Alyssa Thomas of the Phoenix Mercury was suspended for a game for hitting Clark in the throat—inadvertently, according to Thomas—she received death threats, was subjected to racial slurs, and inspired those bad-faith congressional demands for an investigation. “Now we’re being painted as thugs,” Thomas told reporters . In mid-July, Chelsea Gray of the Las Vegas Aces, who is almost as superb a player as Clark, received a vile message after her team lost to the Fever. Gray decided to post it on social media so everyone could see what Black players can deal with when they go against the league’s white darling. You s* a** ugly a** read a message that also called her the N-word. Gray wrote on her post, “People act like we just make this s* up.” That was the backstory when Obama surprised the WNBA All-Stars players by walking in on them during practice for tonight’s game. They were milling around an indoor court at the newly opened Obama Presidential Center on Chicago’s South Side when the man with his name on the building sauntered across the floor in jeans and a white broadcloth shirt to welcome them—and to gently remind them of certain truths: It has taken 30 years of effort by underpaid and unsung athletes for the league to finally arrive as a popular mass spectacle, and no matter what team the players are on, they’re all in that endeavor together. The WNBA’s growing commercial success is based in its relatability and affordability compared with men’s pro leagues, but also in the audience’s sense that it is watching not just a game but the slow triumph of women gaining power for themselves. “People paying attention to your excellence, I think, has been something, for basketball fans generally, a sight to see,” Obama told them. The former president took pains to make clear that he’s a genuine follower of the league. He made small remarks to various players about their seasons as he posed for photos. Then Obama spotted Clark. “Oh hey!” he said. “Caitlin! You’re great!” He leaned in closer, to deliver a more personal message, picked up by a hot mic . “Don’t let all this nonsense get you down,” he told her. “I always say one of the things that was luckiest for me was that I didn’t get famous ’til I was like 45. So I was an old-ass man. I mean, you’re my daughter’s age. And to have that much burden and, you know, nonsense. So don’t lose that joy. The game’s, like, the game. And you’re a hooper. And you hoop.” “I try—sometimes,” she said shyly. “You’re always hooping,” he said. “And you’re on a nice little run right now.” There was a sweetness in the moment, a subtle teaching. In the nicest way, Obama shored Clark up, but also reminded her that she is a greater player and public figure when she just plays the game, accepts the inevitable bad calls and frustrations, and doesn’t let the web-brewed poisons into her blood. Left unspoken was the fact that no one has been subject to more unfairness than Black women who can’t buy a call from refs, and don’t get their own signature sneaker deals, either. Obama chose not to corner Clark on that point. Instead, he gave her grace. And perhaps because he did so, she will have more grace with her opponents—and they will, with her. Clark is a peerless young player who can be a bit of a brat when she gets batted around. She’s learning. “Sometimes, I think, people don’t always realize, like, I’m 23 or 24 years old and I’m trying to navigate a lot of different things while trying to play basketball at the same time,” she told the press after meeting Obama. “So, it was cool to hear that from him and I think, honestly, it’s probably a good reminder for all of us to treat people with respect, treat people with grace.” It was a quietly interesting and complicated encounter, and a heartening reminder of what “presidential” can look like. Clark already knows how to win. But Obama gave her a lesson in how to be winning.

items.title: Leila Djansi questions NFA’s appeal for Film Fund donations
items.description: Ghanaian-American filmmaker Leila Djansi has criticised the National Film Authority’s (NFA) appeal for public donations to the Ghana Film Fund, arguing that the fund should generate investment rather than rely on public contributions. Reacting to the NFA’s fundraising appeal in a Facebook post, Djansi said it was wrong to ask Ghanaians to contribute when structures to make the film industry commercially viable had not been established. “Back to the NFA. why ask Ghanaians to donate instead of using the government’s allocation to generate more money?” she questioned. She added: “A Film Fund should be an investment that generates more investment, not a charity that begs for donations.” The award-winning filmmaker argued that authorities should establish structures that would enable Ghana’s film industry to generate sustainable revenue before seeking public support. “Again, I ask: what structures have been put in place to sustain the industry and ensure these films generate revenue?” she wrote. Djansi also rejected the notion that YouTube could serve as the industry’s long-term economic solution. “YouTube is a platform. It is not an industry. It will not replenish a government film fund,” she stated. According to her, Ghana should stop modelling its film industry on Nigeria’s because the two countries have different market realities. “Nollywood should not be Ghana’s standard. Copying Nigeria contributed to the collapse of Ghana’s industry years ago. Doing it again will not produce a different result. What works for Nigeria will not necessarily work for Ghana. You gotta find your own beat.” She explained that Ghana lacked Nigeria’s population, celebrity ecosystem, distribution network and audience size, making it unrealistic to expect the same results from the YouTube-driven model. Instead, she proposed using the Film Fund to attract international productions through competitive tax incentives and grants tied to minimum spending thresholds. “Use the Film Fund to attract foreign productions through competitive tax incentives and grants. Give them a minimum spend. $1.5 million and up,” she said. Drawing comparisons with film incentive programmes in the United States, Djansi noted that Georgia offers a 35% tax credit for qualifying productions, while New Jersey provides 40%, attracting productions that spend heavily in local economies. She argued that international productions filming in Ghana would spend money on hotels, transport, catering, construction, equipment, locations and local crews, generating revenue that government could reinvest in the Film Fund. “That economic activity generates revenue for the country. Government can then reinvest those returns into the Film Fund, creating a cycle of growth instead of a cycle of fundraising,” she wrote. Djansi also suggested that Ghana should pursue a film industry strategy tailored to its own market, saying: “Instead of chasing Nigeria’s numbers, Ghana should build a model that reflects Ghana’s audience and strengths.” Her latest comments are consistent with views she has expressed previously. In an opinion article published in March 2025, Leila argued that government should “fix foundations before funding Ghana’s film industry”, insisting that proper industry structures must be established before public money is invested in film production. She made a similar argument during an interview on Hitz FM last year where she said she did not believe in establishing a film fund without a viable distribution system, warning that relying on YouTube was not a sustainable business model for Ghanaian filmmakers.

items.title: Contrats d'objectifs 2026 : Le ministre de l'Énergie, des mines et des carrières a un taux de réalisation estimé à 61, 7% au premier semestre
items.description: Le ministre de l'Énergie, des mines et des carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, a été évalué ce samedi 25 juillet 2026 sur son contrat d'objectifs 2026 au 30 juin 2026. A l'issue du processus, il ressort que son département enregistre un taux d'exécution de 61,7 %. ‎Le contrat d'objectifs du ministre de l'Énergie, des mines et des carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba est ficelé autour de cinq objectifs spécifiques et de six orientations prioritaires visant à accélérer les réformes dans les secteurs de l'énergie et des mines. Ainsi, dans le domaine minier, neuf nouvelles coopératives artisanales ont été mises en place dans différentes régions ; quatre couloirs d'exploitation artisanale ont été délimités, en application du nouveau Code minier, afin de mieux organiser les activités et de favoriser une co-habitation harmonieuse entre les exploitations industrielles et artisanales. ‎ « ‎Les opérations de contrôle, de coulage, de pesée et de colisage de l'or se sont poursuivies afin de renforcer le suivi de la production nationale. Au 30 juin 2026, les mines industrielles ont produit environ 26 tonnes d'or fin. La collecte issue des exploitations artisanales et semi-mécanisées, réalisée par la Société nationale des substances précieuses (SONASP), s'élève à environ 29 tonnes, sur une prévision annuelle de 45 tonnes. ‎Le Camarade ministre a également relevé la poursuite de la lutte contre les circuits frauduleux, ainsi que les actions visant à améliorer la connaissance du potentiel minier national et à développer les projets confiés à la Société de participation minière du Burkina Faso (SOPAMIB) », rend compte la Primature à travers sa page Facebook. ‎Dans le secteur énergétique, les capacités nationales de production, de transport et de distribution de l'électricité ont été renforcées tandis que quatre centrales, dont trois thermiques, ont été achevées pour une capacité totale de 126,4 mégawatts. La construction de la centrale solaire de Zagtouli, d'une puissance de 17 mégawatts, a également été finalisée. Les centrales de Komsilga et de Donsin sont, quant à elles, en cours d'achèvement. ‎« Nous avons obtenu un résultat globalement satisfaisant, à mettre à l'actif du personnel du ministère et de l'ensemble des acteurs des secteurs de l'énergie et des mines. Les orientations du camarade Premier ministre nous permettront d'accélérer les chantiers et de renforcer la souveraineté énergétique et minière de notre pays », a, au sortir de l'exercice, réagi le ministre de l'Énergie, des mines et des carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba. Lefaso.net Source : DCRP/Primature

items.title: The ‘Our Day’ Dilemma: A cherished Ghanaian tradition that has become a high-pressure cooker
items.description: The day that was once the most anticipated day on the school calendar, the day filled with laughter, juice boxes, and paper baskets of colour, has become a war zone of outrage. As basic schools across the country officially end the term on Thursday, July 23, 2026, social media has exploded into a heated debate. The trigger? A wave of mounting allegations from frustrated parents claiming that the once beloved end-of-term “Our Day” tradition has been hijacked and turned into financial extortion. For decades in Ghanaian culture, showing gratitude to educators was simple but spontaneous and heart-driven. But recent claims paint a vastly different picture of today’s classrooms where direct solicitations are used. According to reports monitored on social media, parents now report receiving direct messages and phone calls from teachers nudging them to fund end-of-term “appreciation packages.” Some of the requests have reportedly ballooned from small tokens of appreciation to high-ticket items, including home appliances such as microwaves and substantial cash demands. The situation has pushed parents, especially those with wards in private schools, into a corner, fearing their kids will be embarrassed or treated differently if they go to school empty-handed. “Our Day” then and now The controversy stands in stark contrast to the memories of older generations. Gone are the days when ‘Our Day’ meant excitement, laughter, and sharing, not expectations. Growing up, while living with my late grandmother, my school was just behind our house. I could easily read between the lines when classes were about to begin. I would quickly prepare myself and rush off to school, eager to join my friends. Those were our “Syto” days in public schools. Our biggest excitement back then was not about buying gifts for teachers; the real deal lay in “Our Day” celebrations. Going to school with biscuits, drinks, and food packed in beautifully decorated baskets covered with white cloth was the ish of the day. It was a real joy. “When I was in primary school, our biggest excitement was not about buying gifts for teachers. We looked forward to bringing biscuits, drinks, and food packed in beautifully decorated baskets covered with white cloth. That was the real joy. It was never a rule. No parent was forced, and no child felt embarrassed.” Pupils brought small tokens like drinks or biscuits in appreciation of their teachers, who accepted them with utmost pride. But it was a voluntary gesture, as no parent was forced, and no child felt embarrassed because they could not offer a gift to their teacher. It was simply an expression of a show of love and appreciation. But society over time is changing, forcing the meaning attached to Our Day gifts to change too. There is no doubt that teachers deserve to be appreciated. They shoulder bigger responsibilities even beyond the walls of classrooms. They provide guidance and counselling and, in some instances, spend financially on their pupils. Those teachers deserve recognition. For instance, if a parent recognises the influence of a teacher on a ward and showers gifts on him or her willingly, there is absolutely nothing wrong with that. After all, appreciating people for their good deeds is sacrosanct with the Ghanaian upbringing. A small gesture from a grateful heart can mean a lot. But the real problem begins when appreciation becomes an expectation. When parents are asked to exchange expensive gifts such as microwaves or large sums of money, then it raises concerns. Some overburdened parents already struggling to make ends meet will be put under unbearable pressure. A gift should bring happiness, not stress. Some people argue parents who choose private schools over public ones should be ready to meet the expectations that come with them. institutions. While parents certainly want the best for their children, appreciation should never feel like a compulsory payment. Perhaps a better approach is to allow parents to raise specific concerns instead of blaming teachers for their predicaments. If a particular teacher or school makes unreasonable demands, that situation should be addressed directly rather than painting every teacher ‘black’. Because the truth is, many teachers continue to serve with dedication and commitment. At the same time, we should not allow this conversation to destroy our culture of kindness and generosity. Giving has always been part of who we are as Ghanaians. When we are kind and loving to others, God is pleased. So, let us continue to appreciate teachers, but let that appreciation come from the heart — not from pressure, fear or obligation. Perhaps the greatest gift a teacher can receive is not an expensive item wrapped in a package but the appreciation of their patience, sacrifice and hard work that have helped shape the life of a child. Ultimately, the essence of Our Day is not about the gifts. It was always about gratitude, love, and appreciation. Source: Dorcas Abedu-Kennedy

items.title: Bintimodia/Boké : l’ONFPP renforce les capacités de 20 femmes en techniques de maraîchage
items.description: L’Office National de Formation et de Perfectionnement Professionnels (ONFPP) a lancé, le mercredi 22 juillet 2026, une session de formation en techniques de maraîchage au profit de 20 femmes de la sous-préfecture de Bintimodia, dans la préfecture de Boké. Cette formation se déroulera du 22 juillet au 5 août 2026. Cette initiative, qui réunit des participantes issues de huit districts de la commune rurale, s’inscrit dans le cadre des actions de lutte contre la précarité et de promotion de l’autonomisation économique des femmes. À travers cette formation collective théorique et pratique, l’ONFPP entend renforcer les compétences des bénéficiaires afin d'améliorer leurs activités maraîchères et leurs revenus. Dans son allocution de bienvenue, le maire de la Commune rurale de Bintimodia, Mamadou Aziz Diallo, a salué le choix porté sur sa commune pour accueillir cette formation. « Il n'existe pratiquement aucun district de Bintimodia où les femmes ne pratiquent pas le maraîchage. Cependant, elles sont confrontées à de nombreuses difficultés techniques. Je suis convaincu qu'à l'issue de cette formation, elles disposeront des compétences nécessaires pour mieux développer leurs activités. Nous remercions l'ONFPP et souhaitons que d'autres formations soient également organisées au profit des jeunes dans différents domaines », a-t-il dit. Prenant la parole, Aboubacar Keïta, chef d'antenne régionale de l'ONFPP à Boké, a rappelé que la mission de son institution est d'accompagner les jeunes et les femmes vers une meilleure insertion professionnelle. Selon lui, cette formation vise à renforcer les compétences des participantes dans les techniques modernes de production maraîchère, en mettant un accent particulier sur les pratiques agricoles durables, la bonne gestion des cultures et l'amélioration de la qualité des productions. Au nom des bénéficiaires, Aïssatou Camara a exprimé sa gratitude envers l'ONFPP pour cette initiative. Elle a invité les participantes à tirer pleinement profit des enseignements reçus afin de mériter la confiance des autorités et des partenaires de développement. Pour sa part, Daouda Bangoura, formateur de l'atelier, a indiqué que la session se déroulera du 22 juillet au 5 août théorique et pratique Il a précisé qu'elle permettra aux bénéficiaires de maîtriser les techniques de production maraîchère afin de mettre sur le marché local des produits de meilleure qualité. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité de poursuivre l'accompagnement des femmes et des jeunes, dont les capacités techniques et entrepreneuriales constituent un levier essentiel pour le développement local. Il convient de rappeler que l'ONFPP est un établissement public à caractère administratif placé sous la tutelle du ministère de l'Enseignement technique, de la Formation professionnelle et de l'Emploi. Sa mission principale est de contribuer à la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale en matière de formation professionnelle continue et d'apprentissage.
